A banned address receives the page with status 200 and a notice that begins attempts exhausted and shows the hours and minutes left; the notice is built in page.c and shown for the ban of the key and of the /48. The ban of one user on that key is not known to the page, which does not know the user, and the same refusal arrives through RCP. The status is 200 and not a 4xx because an intermediary or the browser may replace the body of an error response, and the sentence the owner must read would vanish.

    !
    No administrator unblock. the ban notice in page.c ends with «The block ends by itself when that time is up: there is no other way back in». That is the owner's decision of 17 Nov 2026: the package ships no administrator unblock. The unit passes no --command-socket and there is no command-line tool; command.c and rcp_unblock() are still in the binary behind that bench option, which the checks switch on with a drop-in, and prove/check-ban.py (check unblock-shipped) records that the package gives the administrator no way to unblock, by design. A banned user waits for the ban to expire. The text of SPECS.md §4.2 still names an unblock command (UNBLOCK <address>) among the ways out: it is not aligned with the decision (see ch. 24 “Appendix C — Known issues and open points”).

    4.9 · The WebTransport layer: SETTINGS, CONNECT, streams and capsules

    webtransport.c is the layer on top of ngtcp2 and nghttp3. It covers three holes: WebTransport cannot be announced through the nghttp3 API; WebTransport streams must be taken away from nghttp3, which would read the session number after 0x41 as a frame length; and the bytes going back on those streams have no road, because nghttp3 never schedules streams it does not know.

    • Both drafts are announced. The setting of draft 02 and the one of draft 07 are both sent: the test client aioquic 1.2 implements the first and browsers look for the second, and an unknown setting is ignored by the other side.
    • HTTP/3 needs three unidirectional streams. open_http3() fails the connection, logged, if the client grants fewer than three.
    • One session per connection. w->session holds the stream id of the CONNECT. WT_CAP_CHANNEL_NS (5 s) starts when the session opens: if the client does not open the control channel in time the session is closed with TIMED_OUT in the closing code (DECISIONS.md §7.17).
    • Client streams are classified by their first bytes (enum flavor): undecided, WebTransport bidirectional (the control channel), HTTP/3 (handed back to nghttp3), WebTransport unidirectional for input (G_UNI_INPUT), for clipboard (G_UNI_CLIPBOARD), lawful but not served, or already judged a violation. The channel is recognised by the high byte of the first RCP type after the preamble: 0x01 is input, 0x02 clipboard; 0x00 (control), 0x03 (video) and 0x04 (audio) on a client unidirectional stream, or any other byte, are violations of RCP.md §2.5. The first bidirectional WebTransport stream becomes the control channel and a second one is a violation.
    • The session number in the preamble is read and logged, not compared with the stream id of the CONNECT (dispatch(), dispatch_uni()). With one session per connection it cannot name another one.
    • The closing capsule goes inside a DATA frame. Written bare, its first byte 0x68 makes the browser read a two-byte HTTP/3 frame type 0x2843, an unknown frame that RFC 9114 requires to ignore; the page would see only the FIN behind it, which closes the session with code 0, the one value RCP forbids. The code is one byte of the u32 (mm above).
    • The capsule is delayed. It is queued only after the send queue of the session has drained, plus WT_CLOSE_WAIT_NS (500 ms): the code comment in close_session() records that browsers process the capsule before the stream bytes sent just ahead of it and throw those away, so the page never saw REJECTED. If the queue does not drain, the capsule leaves all the same after a 3 s backstop.
    • A capsule from the client is accumulated and parsed by closed_by_client() and handed to rcp_closed_by_client(). A code outside 0x01–0x0F is logged as a violation of RCP.md §3.1 and recorded as PROTOCOL_ERROR. The range stops at 0x0F although RCP.md §8.2 and reason_for_82() in rcp.c also accept 0x10: a client closing with 0x10 would be logged as a violation. A real page never sends it.

    Before login, a stranger's connection is cheap to keep and cheap to log. A connection that has never logged in may open at most WT_PRELOGIN_SESSIONS_MAX = 2 WebTransport sessions and make WT_PRELOGIN_REQUESTS_MAX = 8 other HTTP/3 requests before it is closed with H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD; the counters start again at the moment a login is earned. Its log lines are budgeted per address key (WT_PRELOGIN_BURST = 20 lines per WT_PRELOGIN_WINDOW_MS = 10 s, WT_PRELOGIN_KEYS = 128 keys) and for the whole server (WT_PRELOGIN_GLOBAL_BURST = 100), so a flood cannot fill the journal of root. The line of a failed attempt that counts towards the ban and the line of the ban itself are never held back.

    4.10 · Streams, datagrams and the send queue

    Each RCP channel uses the QUIC piece that matches its needs. The design choice that matters most is that a video frame is a stream: a late frame does not hold up the next one, and the server can abandon a frame that is no longer useful with RESET_STREAM so that its unsent bytes never leave.

    On a single stream a slow frame would block all the following ones (head-of-line blocking). On datagrams the server would have to rewrite fragmentation and retransmission, QUIC inside QUIC. One stream per frame gives independence for free, and abandonment for the price of a key frame (see ch. 8 “Quality, degradation and budget”).

    Audio datagrams. A datagram cannot be fragmented, so it must fit in one packet. audio_a_una() builds the datagram: the varint of the session stream id divided by four, then the 12-byte RCP header (type 0x0401, codec, 64-bit instant) and the block. The server caps its datagram at WT_DGRAM_BYTE = 1024 bytes and drops, counted and logged, a block larger than the peer announced in max_datagram_frame_size (a peer that announced zero gets no audio at all, said once in the log). The 1024 is recorded in the code as the largest datagram browsers accepted in a measurement with Chrome and Firefox; the probe is not in this tree. At most WT_DGRAM_MAX = 8 blocks wait to be sent, and a block that has not left within WT_DGRAM_QUIET_MAX_MS = 10 ms of the queue being blocked is dropped and counted. wt_dgram_lost() and wt_dgram_acked() track losses and acknowledgements in pairs, because ngtcp2 can declare a datagram lost and later see it acknowledged, which is reordering and not loss.

    Stream credit for video. The browser grants unidirectional streams to the server at its own pace. The server must survive a refused stream: when credit is missing it drops the frame, but never a key frame, which waits. WT_UNI_RESERVE = 2 streams are left unused by video so the client's own streams are never starved, and at most WT_INFLIGHT_MAX = 32 frames are in flight per session. A frame dropped for lack of credit is invisible to the client (no stream, no gap in the numbering), so the server owes a key frame on its own.

    The send queue. Every byte to send on a stream goes through queue_put(). The queue of a session is capped at WT_QUEUE_MAX = 17 MiB (16 MiB, the largest video frame RCP allows, plus 1 MiB for control messages) and at WT_QUEUE_ITEMS_MAX = 16384 elements; touching either cap is logged and the item is not queued. When a stream is flow-blocked only that stream is skipped for the pass, at most WT_BLOCKED_MAX = 64 per pass, so one slow frame does not block the others inside the queue.

    !
    The send buffer belongs to us until it is acknowledged. ngtcp2_conn_writev_stream() does not copy the bytes: it keeps the caller's pointer and rereads it to retransmit. A queue element therefore has two states: delivered (all bytes handed to ngtcp2, memory kept) and dead (freed), reached only from an acknowledgement covering the bytes, the closing of the stream or its reset. Freeing a frame once it was serialised would hand garbage to a retransmission, or crash the server on a large frame.

    4.11 · Idle timeout, keep-alive PINGs and the dead line

    Several clocks watch a connection, and they measure different things. They are listed here so that nobody mistakes one for another.

    Transport PINGs. keepalive_rule() arms ngtcp2_conn_set_keep_alive_timeout() when the RCP state is anything but finished and switches it off when the session ends. The interval is keepalive_ns(): half of the dead-line silence when the detector is on, so 5 s with the defaults, otherwise 10 s. Without them nothing travels while the server waits for the credentials (RCP gives 60 s for them) and the 30 s idle timeout would kill the connection, and the liveness margin would belong to the browser's own keep-alive. A PING carries no information and has no reply to interpret, so it is not the application heartbeat that RCP forbids.

    i
    Comment and code disagree. the comment in rcp.c above rcp_sign_of_life() says the PINGs are on only during the credentials window. The code in keepalive_rule() arms them for every state but finished, and that is what this manual describes (the code wins).

    Why the silence clock looks at packets, not at RCP bytes. A user who only reads sends nothing on RCP; counting RCP bytes would detach them after 30 s while the connection is alive. The 30 s clock looks at the last decrypted and authenticated packet instead. The much longer clocks that watch what the user does (30 minutes of inactivity, 60 minutes of abandonment) are described in ch. 5 “The RCP/1 protocol”.

    The dead line. dead_line_judge() runs once per round and decides on two causes. Silence: the client showed no packet for the threshold while at least two packets of ours went unanswered; the time alone is not enough, because a still desktop in which neither side speaks is legitimately quiet. Stall: no video byte left for the threshold while there was video to send; the count restarts whenever something goes out or nothing is waiting. The loss ratio from ngtcp2 is computed but is only a witness in the log, because on a line that reorders it measures reordering. When it fires, dead_line_fires() writes one log line with all the numbers and sets the application error H3_NO_ERROR with the text dead line, and transport_expired() sends a single CONNECTION_CLOSE and marks the connection dead. No RCP FAREWELL is sent: the line by hypothesis does not carry it, and the user comes back in by hand. The detector is on by default; --no-dead-line switches it off and the start-up line says so. It is the one clock that throws out someone who is working if it is mistuned.

    4.12 · Congestion, pacing and the video queue

    QUIC measures the line continuously. REMOTIX uses that measurement and adds mechanisms of its own on the video queue; the policy built on them is the subject of the chapter ch. 8 “Quality, degradation and budget”.

    The threshold and the regulator are on together by default; with the threshold off the delta queue empties at every frame and the regulator can never trigger, which the start-up line says. The code comments record a declared price measured with benches that are not in this tree: up to 160 ms of extra delay on a bad line and none on a healthy one. This manual does not repeat those measurements as verified for this version.

    4.13 · One connection from first packet to close

    One QUIC connection carries at most one WebTransport session and one RCP session. The steps follow a connection from its first datagram to its close; the RCP steps inside are in ch. 5 “The RCP/1 protocol”.

    1. First packets. transport_read() receives with recvmsg (with the destination address from IP_PKTINFO or IPV6_PKTINFO), ngtcp2_accept checks the Initial, and the admission pipeline of 4.5 “Admission of new connections, Retry and Stateless Reset” runs. accept_conn() creates a struct connection with an 18-byte signed server connection id and the textual source address as provenance, the key of the ban and of the logs.
    2. 1-RTT keys ready. cb_recv_tx_key() calls wt_app_ready(), which runs open_http3(): three unidirectional streams of the server (control, QPACK encoder, QPACK decoder) with the rewritten SETTINGS.
    3. CONNECT. open_session() accepts the session on /rcp/1 and the 5-second deadline for the control channel starts.
    4. Control channel. The first bidirectional WebTransport stream from the client becomes RCP's control channel; rcp_open() creates the rcp_session with the provenance, and the transport keep-alive is armed.
    5. Life. Stream data goes to rcp_receive(), rcp_receive_input() or rcp_receive_clipboard() according to the class of the stream. Frames, audio blocks and cursor shapes coming from the per-user child are fanned out by user name (wt_video_broadcast(), wt_audio_broadcast(), wt_cursor_broadcast()), each reaching only the connections whose RCP user is that user.
    6. Close. RCP decides why (ch. 5 “The RCP/1 protocol”), and the WebTransport layer sends the capsule. The farewell of a graphical session that is over goes through wt_dismiss_user_session_over(), which chooses which connections of the user receive it (3.4 “From password to admission”). At shutdown transport_dismiss_all() says goodbye to every session with SERVER_CLOSING and the loop runs until the queues drain or a time budget (4 s in main.c) expires. The log line of the connection's end, “connection with X closed (n left)”, carries the reason (4.14 “Why a connection closed”).
    +
    Verdict routing. the PAM verdict reaches the right connection through transport_verdict_as(): the helper returns a ticket number, the transport offers it to every live session, and exactly one takes it. A verdict that finds nobody is counted as an orphan and not lost: the connection died while PAM was answering, and transport_awaits_verdict() lets the caller skip starting a desktop for nobody.

    4.14 · Why a connection closed

    A browser that cannot open a session says one thing, “Opening handshake failed”, whatever went wrong. The log says who closed the connection and why, with one line per connection: connection with ADDRESS closed (n left) — …. The text is written by close_why() in transport.c, from what ngtcp2 recorded, and changes no behaviour and keeps no data of the client beyond the address that was already there.

    A browser that connected with a wrong fingerprint produces the PEER closed it: transport error CRYPTO 0x12e = TLS alert 46 certificate_unknown and TLS handshake NOT completed. A browser killed with SIGKILL gives, 30 s later, “dropped without a CONNECTION_CLOSE: idle timeout (silence)”. Connections that never logged in are limited to the number of lines per window of BIRTH_LINES: beyond it the line goes to the detail level, with the same text; the closing of a connection that did log in is always written.

    !
    The client's clock. The certificate of a session is made valid from one hour before the moment it is created (notBefore = now minus 3600 s, certificates.c), and the browser checks that date against its own clock. A client device whose clock is more than an hour behind the server's sees the certificate as “not yet valid”, and the browser says only Opening handshake failed. It is not a defect: a very wrong clock breaks every secure site anyway, and the margin is not widened. Requirement: the clock of the client device must be right. The closing line above is how the cause is read in the log.

    4.15 · What was verified for the transport

    What is known about the transport at this version comes from three sources, and it helps to keep them apart: the automatic rounds of the checks in prove/ (the four virtual machines, 26 and 27 Nov 2026), what the owner tried by hand on the virtual machines and on real machines, and what is only in the code. Because QEMU's user network shows every client as 10.0.2.2, the ban check can only try the ban of that one address (check-ban.py).

    Chapter 5

    The RCP/1 protocol

    5.1 · RCP/1 in one page and where its specification lives

    RCP/1, the Remotix Control Protocol, is what the page and the server say to each other inside the WebTransport session. Its specification is docs/RCP.md, written before the code and precise enough to prove an implementation wrong; this chapter does not copy it. It records what src/rcp.c does at each message, so that a maintainer can go from a message name to the function that handles it, and says where the code and the specification differ.

    What the module knows. rcp.c knows RCP and nothing else: no sockets, no QUIC, no clock of its own, no PAM, no compositor. Time arrives as a parameter (rcp_time() and the now argument of each call), bytes leave through hooks, so a test can make time run as it wants. Everything it needs from the product reaches it through the function pointers of rcp_hooks in rcp.h: sending on the control channel, closing the session, the log, the PAM question, opening and writing video and clipboard streams, the five input injections, resizing the stage, keyboard layouts, the local-session test, terminating the session and a few more. A missing hook is logged and never treated as a client violation. The host of the hooks is webtransport.c (the stream ones) and main.c (the ones that reach the child, PAM and the budget). The comment in rcp.h that says the hooks are «three, and no more» is stale: there are twenty-nine.

    The client. The only client is the page, src/page.html, which speaks RCP in JavaScript. The server and the page are two readings of the same specification written by the same people; the document RCP.md is the referee, and a test that wants to prove either wrong should read the document and not the other program. The test programs that did this in the earlier work are not part of this tree.

    5.2 · Message map: every type and the function that handles it

    Every message has a 16-bit type. The high byte is the channel: 0x00 control, 0x01 input, 0x02 clipboard, 0x03 video, 0x04 audio. The table gives, for every type the code knows, who sends it, in which RCP state it is legal, and the function to read. Control messages are all dispatched by one switch in drain_at(); the state is the enum enum state (wait-hello, wait-credentials, wait-verdict, wait-attach, active, detached-by-silence, finished).

    All integers are big-endian, no field is aligned and nothing is padded. A string is a 16-bit length followed by that many bytes. The reader helpers of rcp.c are named le_u8(), le_u16(), le_u32() and le_str(); the le is the Italian legge («reads») and not «little-endian», which is easy to misread. The writers are sc_byte(), sc_u16(), sc_u32(), sc_u64() and sc_str().

    The frame header, written by rcp_video_open(), is 28 bytes: u16 type, u16 codec (1 = HEVC, 2 = AV1, 3 = H.264, see rcp_codec_negotiated(); the server never negotiates AV1), u32 canvas width and height, u32 frame number (it starts at 1 and skips 0 on wrap, next_number()), u64 instant in microseconds and u32 id of the last input injected (0 means none). There is no length: the end of the stream is the end of the frame. The frame is capped at V_CAP = 16 MiB including the header; a larger one is refused with RCP_VIDEO_TOO_LARGE and the caller re-encodes at lower quality. A stream that cannot be completed is ended with RESET_STREAM and never with a FIN, because a FIN would make a short frame look valid.

    5.3 · Framing and the rigor rule as implemented

    The first rule of RCP is that an implementation that receives something it does not understand closes with PROTOCOL_ERROR and writes in the log what it did not understand. It does not ignore, guess or carry on. In rcp.c that rule is concentrated in a few functions.

    1. Accumulate, bounded. rcp_receive() appends the bytes to a per-session buffer through accumulate(). The buffer grows on demand and only up to MAX_ACCUMULATION, equal to MAX_MESSAGE = 1 MiB, framing included (MAX_BODY = 1 MiB minus the 6-byte header). A body above it is PROTOCOL_ERROR before any allocation.
    2. Header. drain_at() reads the 6-byte header: u16 type, u32 body length. On the control channel the high byte of the type must be 0x00. The length is checked before the body is waited for.
    3. Length against the fields, before any effect. measure_fields() reads the body a second time just to measure the fields that type must have; if the declared length differs, the connection is closed before the message has any effect on the wire or the state. It is a second reader of the same layouts: whoever changes a body in a handler changes it here too, and the check after the switch (l.i != lung) is what notices when they do not. A body that is too short is left to the handler, which can say which field was missing.
    4. The rate gate for the control messages that have one (below), then the switch on the type with the state check of each case: a message in the wrong state is PROTOCOL_ERROR with the text «X in the wrong state».
    5. Text rules. Names are lower-case letters, digits, . and _ (valid_name()); values are printable (printable_text()); a FAREWELL detail must be valid UTF-8 (valid_utf8()); a password with an embedded zero byte is refused because what arrives and what would be judged would differ.

    What closing means in bytes. dismiss() is the one road: it logs the reason, state and detail, releases the held keys and buttons (release_on_detach()), sends FAREWELL (reason byte and detail string) if the channel is still usable, frees the attach slot, sets the state finished and calls the close hook, which makes webtransport.c close the WebTransport session with the application error code equal to the reason (see ch. 4 “Transport”). The reason therefore travels twice: in the message, and in the close code, so it arrives even when the control channel is broken. Code 0 is never used. reject() does the same for REJECTED, which carries the reason itself and is not followed by a FAREWELL. rcp_violation() is for faults the host sees (a stream in the wrong direction, two bidirectional streams): the same close, with the control channel still usable in most cases.

    After the end. Bytes that arrive on the control channel when the state is already finished are judged by judge_after_end(), on messages and not on the first bytes of the piece: a FAREWELL that crossed the server's own close is the client doing what the specification demands and is not a violation, while any other message after the end (for example a second CREDENTIALS after REJECTED) is logged as a violation. Nothing is sent back.

    RCP.md §3 carries the list of declared exceptions to the rigor rule. The table above is the list of places in the code that write «TOLERANCE» or «DECLARED FALLBACK» and does not claim to equal it exactly; a maintainer who adds a tolerance is expected to add its row to RCP.md §3 in the same change.

    5.4 · The handshake step by step

    The handshake has five steps and runs on the control channel. Every message that arrives in a state that does not expect it is a PROTOCOL_ERROR. Three properties follow from the order: the server proves who it is (TLS with the pinned certificate) before the password leaves the browser; authentication comes before attachment, so whoever is not admitted cannot even name a session; and the canvas is agreed at attach time.

    The clock s->since restarts after each message that is fully processed, and ch. 4 “Transport” adds a fifth deadline in front of these: WT_CAP_CHANNEL_NS = 5 s from the WebTransport session to the opening of the control channel, which closes the session with TIMED_OUT without a FAREWELL, because the control channel does not exist.

    5.5 · HELLO, HERE_I_AM and capability negotiation

    HELLO carries the highest major version the client speaks and its capabilities: a count and pairs of name and value strings. handle_hello() is the function. A version other than RCP_VERSION = 1 closes with INCOMPATIBLE_VERSION. The version lives in two places that must coincide, the path /rcp/1 (checked by open_session(), wrong path: HTTP 404) and this field.

    A name that appears twice is a violation, a name that is not lower-case-and-digits is a violation, an empty value is a violation, and so is a value above 256 bytes or not printable. An unknown name is ignored (that is how future versions will talk) but the repetition of unknown names is tracked up to MAX_SEEN = 64 of them. HERE_I_AM declares the server's lists, not the choice: video.codec, video.depth, audio.codec, clipboard.text = yes, and video.pace = yes only when the server runs with --decoder-pace and the session's host connected the pace hook. If the codec list is empty because no card can encode, the server calls the codec-retry hook once (the card may have appeared after start-up) and then answers NOTHING_IN_COMMON; the package also refuses a new installation on a machine without a render node.

    i
    No bench function in the product. the bench function (BENCH_MARK, bench.mark) is compiled only with REMOTIX_BENCH. debian/rules refuses to package if BENCH_ON in rcp.c is not 0, and build/build-deb.sh has a check that the installed binary does not contain it. In the installed server bench.mark is an unknown capability and 0x000F is an unknown message type, so it closes the session with PROTOCOL_ERROR.

    5.6 · CREDENTIALS, the verdict and the fixed second

    handle_credentials() receives user and password in one message. Both are length-checked (user 1 to 256, password 1 to 1024 bytes), the user must be printable UTF-8, and the password must contain no zero byte. The password is wiped with explicit_bzero on every path. Nothing is judged by the server itself: the verdict comes from PAM, through the helper process, and arrives asynchronously.

    1. The limiter first. login_reserve() books the attempt against the three levels (below). If the address or the user is banned, or too many attempts are in flight, the reason is set to TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS and PAM is not asked at all. The table has a bottom: a full table, or a quota of bans, refuses without evicting a ban; only for a key that logged in within the last 30 days is the least valuable ban dropped as a last resort (lcreate(), logged).
    2. PAM. Otherwise the ask_verify hook sends the question to the helper and the session waits in wait-verdict. If the question could not be sent, or there is no helper, the answer is a refusal that is the server's own (refusal_is_ours): it goes out as SESSION_UNSERVABLE, the booking is given back, and it does not count towards a ban, because a ban for a defect of the server would be the worst possible diagnosis.
    3. The verdict. rcp_verdict_as() checks four things before it touches cred_good: the session is in wait-verdict, a verdict was asked for, the ticket is this session's own, and it is consumed once. It resolves the attempt in the limiter and, on success, replaces the typed user name by the system's canonical spelling. rcp_verdict_lost() handles the helper dying before it answers.
    4. The wait. rcp_time() sends the answer only after a floor measured from the arrival of CREDENTIALS: FIXED_DELAY = 1000 ms for a success and for refusals whose reason is not WRONG_CREDENTIALS, and REJECT_FLOOR = 2500 ms for a WRONG_CREDENTIALS refusal, so that a name in the denied list (refused at once) cannot be told from a wrong password (PAM's own failure delay) by timing. If PAM answers later than the floor, PAM paces the answer.
    5. The answer. Success sends ADMITTED (empty body) and enters wait-attach. Failure calls reject() with the reason: WRONG_CREDENTIALS for every refusal of PAM (wrong password, no such user, locked account, denied list), TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS for the limiter, SESSION_UNSERVABLE for a refusal that is the server's. A refusal the host decides after a PAM yes (the budget, a local session, the desktop that cannot start, including a compositor that is not installed: session_missing_component()) is kept by rcp_dismiss_login() until the same floor has passed, then sent as a FAREWELL. A connection that was already ADMITTED but is still inside the fixed second (rcp_admitted_waiting(), state wait-verdict with no verdict expected, good credentials and no farewell held) can also be given a held 0x10 or 0x0E by wt_dismiss_user_session_over(): it leaves in the place of ADMITTED.

    The ban is progressive per level: LADDER_MS = 15 minutes, then 1 hour, then 12 hours, and the memory of earlier bans is forgotten after FORGET_MS = 24 hours without one. A successful login resets only the failures of that user on that key. At most MAX_PER_USER_IN_FLIGHT = 2 attempts per user and key are in flight. The table holds MAX_ATTEMPTS = 256 entries, of which BAN_QUOTA = 160 are for bans; once the quota is full, keys that never logged in share a common counter of UNKNOWN_LIMIT = 5 failures in UNKNOWN_WINDOW_MS = 5 minutes, and keys that logged in within 30 days (GOOD_KEYS = 64, GOOD_AGE) always find a place. The ban survives a restart: save_ban() writes it to the file given by --ban-file and rcp_ban_load() reads it back, with an absolute time because the process clock is monotonic. The file never holds a typed user name (an HMAC) and the log writes a name that is not a user of the machine as a short tag. The full description of these defences is the subject of ch. 13 “Login and its defences”.

    !
    The floor of a refusal is 2.5 s. RCP.md §4.4 and §4.4-bis speak of a fixed second before the answer; the code's floor for a refused WRONG_CREDENTIALS is 2.5 s (REJECT_FLOOR). A client that times the answer against one second will not see the refusal in time. prove/check-ban.py judges the code's number and says so in its header.

    5.7 · ATTACH and SESSION as implemented

    ATTACH asks for a desktop: the canvas the client would like (width, height), the view it will draw into (width, height) and the keyboard layout name. handle_attach() is a sequence of checks, in this order; the first failure ends the session.

    Then SESSION goes out: one state byte (1 = a new desktop, 2 = the stage was already there, from the session_resumed hook), the granted canvas (two u32) and the desktop name string from the desktop hook (unknown if none). The session becomes active, the first frame is owed as a key frame, apply_layout() asks the stage for the layout and the recanvas hook tells the stage the canvas. The video stream may only open after SESSION, and the client may open its input stream only after receiving it; a video stream arriving before SESSION would be a refused frame with RCP_VIDEO_BEFORE_SESSION.

    5.8 · Key frames, canvas, view and layout messages

    Video is compressed with prediction between frames, so losing a delta frame ruins every following frame until a key frame arrives. The protocol never retransmits a frame; it abandons one and owes a key frame. The state that decides is needs_key in the session, set by key_needed() and cleared by key_paid().

    A delta is refused by rcp_video_open() with RCP_VIDEO_NEEDS_KEY while a key frame is owed; asking rcp_video_needs_key() before encoding avoids the wasted work. The numbers 1 and above grow by one per frame, so a gap in numbering is what a client reads as loss and answers with REQUEST_KEY carrying the last number it decoded.

    Canvas. FIT_CANVAS is the only message that changes the canvas. In the T_FIT_CANVAS case of drain_at() the request is clamped by rcp_size_allowed() and by the client's video.max_size, refused if it falls below the minimum, checked against the budget (canvas_fits hook), passed to the stage (recanvas hook) and left in flight. There is no answer yet: the answer is the first frame at the new size, and if it does not arrive within RCP_CANVAS_WAIT_MS = 3000 ms the answer is NOT_NOW (canvas_expires()). CANVAS carries an outcome (1 = FITTED, 2 = REFUSED), a reason and the canvas in force after the message; one CANVAS is sent for every FIT_CANVAS.

    View and layout. VIEW stores the new size of the client's window and logs it; the canvas does not change and nothing is encoded differently, the client rescales. Any size from 1 by 1 up is legal, odd included; a zero side is a violation. LAYOUT changes the keyboard layout with the session open: a malformed name is a violation, the layout already in force asks nothing of the stage, and a layout the machine does not know keeps the old one and does not close the session (at ATTACH it does, because there is no session to save yet).

    5.9 · Input, clipboard and cursor messages

    The input channel is one client unidirectional stream, opened after SESSION and kept open. Every message has the common 12 bytes (u32 id and u64 instant, I_COMMON) and a fixed length per type, so a wrong length is known as soon as the 6-byte header has arrived; the buffer is I_ACCUMULATION = 32 bytes and a megabyte announced here gets a farewell after six bytes. rcp_receive_input() refuses bytes before SESSION, a second input stream, and a type whose high byte is not 0x01.

    • The id of an input message must be above the last id of the whole channel, not per type. Zero is reserved (it means no input in the frame header). A gap is legitimate because messages over the rate are dropped.
    • Each type is validated (button and key state must be 0 or 1, a letter must be a Unicode scalar value, a pointer outside the canvas is a violation, except for CANVAS_GRACE = 1000 ms after a canvas change, when it is clamped to the new canvas), then injected through the five hooks input_pointer, input_button, input_wheel, input_letter and input_position. Without the hooks the message is valid and not injected, and the session holds.
    • A valid input message sets the time of the last gesture (last_input), which is what the 30-minute inactivity clock measures. The control messages REQUEST_KEY and PACE do not count as gestures.
    • A release of a button or key that the server saw pressed is never dropped by the rate gate (input_admit()), so a key cannot stay stuck down because of a rate limit. When a session ends, held keys and buttons are released (release_on_detach()).
    • Details of the injection are in ch. 10 “Input”.

    Clipboard. Each transfer is a short-lived unidirectional stream opened by the side that sends. CLIPBOARD_ANNOUNCE says «I have new text» with its byte length (at most RCP_CLIPBOARD_CAP = 1 000 000), CLIPBOARD_ASK asks for it, CLIPBOARD_TEXT carries it. handle_clipboard() rejects a transfer number of 0, a text that was never announced or asked, a length that does not match the announcement and invalid UTF-8; at most A_STREAM_MAX = 8 clipboard streams may be open together, and a pending paste request that the client never answers is dropped after CLIPBOARD_BACKSTOP = 8000 ms (rcp_time()). The first CLIPBOARD_ASK_FREE = 2 requests for the same announcement are served whatever the rate, because a lost ask would make the next one a violation. See ch. 11 “Audio and clipboard”.

    Cursor. The position of the pointer belongs to the client, which draws the pointer itself; only the shape travels, from the server on the control channel (rcp_cursor_shape()). It is not sent before SESSION. The caller must bring exactly width times height times 4 bytes, and the two sizes are zero together or not at all; both would otherwise make the page close the session, so the server refuses to send them and logs why.

    5.10 · Rate limits on a connected client

    After login every message that passes the checks does work on the single thread of the main loop, shared by all users. A client with a valid password, or a modified page, could send them as fast as the link carries them, so each kind has a token bucket per session (msgrate.h). A message over its bucket is consumed without effect and counted; one summary line per MSG_WINDOW_MS = 10 s says how many were dropped, and at most MSG_LINES_PER_WINDOW = 10 lines of one kind are written per window.

    • The rates are wide on purpose: far above a gaming mouse at 1000 Hz or the automatic typing of a password manager, so no person meets them.
    • Last one wins. VIEW, LAYOUT and PACE over the rate are not lost: the newest of each kind is kept and applied when the bucket has a token (lww_apply()), so a stale layout never comes back over a newer one.
    • FIT_CANVAS over the rate is answered CANVAS REFUSED with NOT_NOW, because the specification wants one answer per request.
    • Not limited: the handshake messages, FAREWELL and TERMINATE_SESSION. The clipboard is outside msgrate.h classes but has a bucket of its own in rcp.c (CLIPBOARD_PER_SECOND = 10, CLIPBOARD_BURST = 20, clipboard_over_rate()): a CLIPBOARD_ANNOUNCE over it is consumed without effect, and so is a CLIPBOARD_ASK after the first two for the same announcement. The header comment of msgrate.h still says the clipboard is not limited; the code wins.
    • The gates are active only in active, and a kept message that is being applied again is not charged twice (replaying).

    Other ceilings. A message is at most 1 MiB; a frame at most 16 MiB; a clipboard transfer 1 000 000 bytes; a cursor shape 256 pixels a side (enforced upstream, and double-checked against the message cap). Before login the limits of the transport apply (ch. 4 “Transport”): connection caps, handshake rates, the budget of log lines, and the deadlines above. A client that opens more than A_STREAM_MAX clipboard streams loses one that has no message in progress (logged); only when all eight are halfway through a message is it a violation (clipboard_slot()).

    5.11 · Clocks of an attached session

    Four clocks govern an attached session on the RCP side; the clocks of the transport (idle timeout, PINGs, the dead line) are in ch. 4 “Transport”. Silence and inactivity measure different things: the first asks whether the client is there, the second whether the user is.

    The silence clock looks at packets and not at RCP bytes because a user who only reads sends nothing on RCP; counting RCP bytes detached them after thirty seconds while the connection was alive. The clock stays RCP's own: it does not rely on QUIC's idle timeout, which is negotiated. The price is that a client alive on the wire with a dead page keeps the slot, and the ghost eviction exists to shorten the case of a client that really vanished. The transport PINGs make the packets arrive on a still scene.

    i
    Comment and code disagree. the rcp_sign_of_life() comment says the PINGs are on only in the credentials window; keepalive_rule() arms them for every state but finished. The code wins.

    5.12 · FAREWELL, REJECTED and the sixteen reasons

    Whoever closes sends FAREWELL with a reason before closing the WebTransport session, if the control channel is usable, and repeats the reason as the close code. The reasons are one numbering shared by FAREWELL, REJECTED and the close code (enum in rcp.h, RCP.md §8.2). The table says which code in this tree sends each one.

    The two ends of the closing. The WebTransport layer sends the closing capsule after the send queue has drained and a further 500 ms, so the farewell is not lost (ch. 4 “Transport”). A page that closes sends the code in its own closing capsule, which closed_by_client() validates (codes 0x01 to 0x0F) and passes to rcp_closed_by_client(), which frees the slot at once rather than waiting for the transport to finish. A page that sends FAREWELL first is handled in the T_FAREWELL case: reason and detail are validated (reason between 0x01 and 0x10, detail valid UTF-8), the keys are released, the slot freed and the session closed with the same reason.

    Order for logout. TERMINATE_SESSION is the only message with which the client ends the graphical session. The server sends FAREWELL 0x10 first and only then calls the terminate_session hook, because when the compositor dies the stage dies with it and a farewell sent afterwards would reach nobody. The same code is sent to the other clients of that user when the desktop's own logout ends the session (main.c, through wt_dismiss_user_session_over(), which skips connections that are still waiting for PAM).

    What each kind of fault gets. All the faults below end the RCP session; they differ in what the client is told.

    5.13 · Where the code departs from RCP.md

    RCP.md is the referee and, where the code differs, the difference is recorded here instead of being hidden. None of the following changes the message formats on the wire.

    RCP.md also contains text that describes the earlier versions of the rules next to the current ones (for example the three-attempt twelve-hour ban of the first form beside the progressive ban of the second). Read §4.4-bis together with DECISIONS-11 §11.53; when they disagree with rcp.c the code wins.

    5.14 · What was verified about RCP

    What is known about RCP in this version comes from the checks in prove/, which drive real browsers through the page, and from the source. The checks were run on Ubuntu 26.04 in the round of 26 and 27 November 2026 on the four virtual machines (GNOME 125 PASS and the known pkexec FAIL, KDE, XFCE and LXQt 126 PASS; 1.2 “What was verified and what was not”). They exercise the handshake with a real login, attach and reattach, the second connection of the same user (ALREADY_ACTIVE_REMOTELY), logout (SESSION_TERMINATED), several users at once, input, clipboard, the ban (prove/check-ban.py) and a dropped network.

    A consequence for a maintainer: the strict parser has been read carefully for this manual and run only against the page, which sends well-formed messages. Changing a message body means changing the handler, the entry in measure_fields(), the page, and RCP.md together.

    Chapter 6

    Screen capture

    6.1 · Capture at a glance: one contract, three compositor families

    REMOTIX does not grab a physical screen. Every user has a desktop session of their own, started by REMOTIX with a compositor that has no monitor (ch. 3 “Startup and life cycle”), and the capture reads that compositor's virtual output. On Ubuntu 26.04 there are three compositor families behind the four desktops (Ubuntu with GNOME 50, Kubuntu with KDE Plasma 6.6, Xubuntu with XFCE, Lubuntu with LXQt), and they deliver frames in two opposite directions. GNOME and KDE push frames through a PipeWire node; labwc, the compositor REMOTIX runs under XFCE and LXQt, has no node and every frame is asked for with the wlroots screencopy protocol. A single module, capture.c, hides the difference from child.c.

    Which family is in use is decided once per process by desktop_session() and, for the labwc family, by session_on_wlroots() (both in session.h; see ch. 12 “The four desktops”). In child.c the stage mount tests session_on_wlroots() first, then the KDE case, then GNOME, and opens the capture with capture_start_wlr() or capture_start() accordingly. There is no per-compositor switch inside capture.c: where a compositor cannot do something, the behaviour is the same for everyone that cannot.

    i
    Two labwc programs. two different labwc programs are in play. XFCE and LXQt run the distribution's labwc (0.9.3-1 in Ubuntu's universe), a Recommends of the package, not a hard dependency (debian/control); without it those two desktops cannot start, and since 18 Nov 2026 the server refuses the login with the reason 0x0E before a child is born (session_missing_component() in session.c, called from main.c; the check exists only for XFCE and LXQt). KDE runs REMOTIX's own labwc, /usr/libexec/remotix/labwc, shipped inside the package (labwc 0.9.3 with wlroots 0.19.2 and a small patch, linked statically). If that file is missing KDE still starts, with KWin in its --virtual mode, as a declared fallback. Both cases are in 6.4 “KDE: the KWin screencast protocol and the nested KWin”.

    6.2 · The capture contract

    The mandate written at the top of capture.h is to deliver a frame with the declared buffer type, never a deduced one. Three rules from the earlier REMOTIX generations survive in the code, and each one exists because breaking it produces no error at all.

    The negotiated facts are exposed in CaptureDelivery (read with capture_delivery()), in four groups that downstream code reads instead of recomputing:

    • buffer type: the requested type (requested_route, buffer_requested) and the declared one (buffer_declared) are separate fields, so what arrives is the answer to the question REMOTIX asked, not a discovery about the compositor;
    • bits per channel: from the negotiated format, and 0 means unknown;
    • geometry: size, the stride read from the chunk (stride_read says whether it is a fact or still empty) and the DRM modifier;
    • colour: range, matrix, transfer and primaries as the producer declares them, «not declared» included, plus what REMOTIX measures on the pixels (minimum and maximum per channel, black, uniform).

    The pixel measurement (measure_pixels()) is diagnostic only. It runs on the first frame and then at most every PIXEL_SCAN_EVERY_MS = 500 ms. measured_pixels sits beside the results so that «not black» and «not looked at» cannot be confused: on an unmeasured frame nero and uniform are false, and false would otherwise read as «it is not black». The comments of capture.h give the reason for the cadence as a measured cost of 5.34 ms out of a 21.6 ms path (25 %) when the scan ran on every frame; that figure comes from the comment, not from a run of this tree.

    !
    Real-time thread. the PipeWire callbacks run on PipeWire's own real-time thread (pw_thread_loop). Nothing may wait inside them, capture_stop() must not be called from the end callback, and the pixels live only for the duration of the callback: the copy into REMOTIX's buffer is made there, and frames that arrive while nobody is waiting are only counted.

    CaptureStopped also carries the timing of the stretch that precedes the encoder, in microseconds of CLOCK_MONOTONIC: arrival_us (when the frame was parked), copy_us (the memcpy in the callback), alloc_us (0 when the slot buffer was reused), in_slot_us (how long the frame waited for a taker) and measure_us. They are not filled for a frame delivered to the on_frame callback, where there is no slot and no copy.

    The damage regions (SPA_META_VideoDamage) are information about how much changed, not a condition for reading the buffer. The comment of capture.h records a measurement of 12 Aug 2026 (Mutter 48.7 on Debian, memory path, 410 frames) in which damage was partial on every frame and the buffer was nevertheless whole in every one. At most CAPTURE_DAMAGE_MAX = 16 regions travel with a frame; beyond that the frame counts as entirely damaged, the safe case. damage_classify() tells three cases apart: damage absent (the producer says nothing, the frame counts), empty (the producer declares that nothing changed) and present.

    6.3 · GNOME: the Mutter D-Bus sequence

    On GNOME REMOTIX talks to Mutter's direct D-Bus interfaces, org.gnome.Mutter.RemoteDesktop and org.gnome.Mutter.ScreenCast, on the user's session bus, not to xdg-desktop-portal. The portal asks permission of a user sitting at the screen, and a headless session has nobody there.

    The order admits no permutation, and each wrong order is punished with a different message that never says «wrong order»: the comment of mutter.h records that starting the control session before step 2 gives «Remote desktop session already started» and starting the capture with Session.Start gives «Must be started from remote desktop session». Closing follows the same logic in reverse: mutter_close() stops the control session and the capture follows it. The PipeWire node is announced by a signal emitted during Stream.Start, so mutter.c subscribes to PipeWireStreamAdded before calling it.

    The virtual monitor is mounted by the program every time the stage is mounted, never by configuration: session.c starts gnome-shell --headless --no-x11 without a --virtual-monitor argument, so the session has no monitor until REMOTIX asks for one. Our monitor is identified by name, never by index or size: mutter_find_monitor() compares the connectors before and after RecordVirtual and the product name, and if they do not agree on exactly one new monitor the answer is «unknown», not a guess. It has to be called once the stream is active, because Mutter creates the monitor when a consumer starts reading.

    !
    Scale guard. with org.gnome.desktop.interface scaling-factor set to 2 the stream keeps the requested pixels but the logical monitor gets scale 2.0, and its layout is the coordinate space of input: the pointer would land elsewhere with no log line. mutter_our_scale() reads the scale of our monitor; the child does not take the stage while it is not 1.0. Since 19 Nov 2026 the session first makes the case rare and then tries to repair it. (1) session.c writes org.gnome.desktop.interface scaling-factor = 1 into the session's dconf database and locks it (ch. 12 “The four desktops”). (2) If the scale read is not 1, the child tries once mutter_scale_to_one(): GetCurrentState then ApplyMonitorsConfig with method 1 (temporary), keeping the current mode, passing layout-mode only when the compositor reports supports-changing-layout-mode, and only in the simple case of one logical monitor, which is ours. The user's monitors.xml is not touched, so a local login finds the user's own scale again. Each of the three synchronous calls may wait up to WAIT_CALL_MS = 15 s. (3) If the scale is still not 1, the child sets p.fatal, the parent answers the clients with 0x0E (stage_refused_by_child() in main.c) and the graphical session is closed, retried every 10 s if the closing fails. The log lines are «scale back to 1 (temporary, the user's monitors.xml untouched)» and «the user's scale … is IGNORED in the remote session». The old one-line cure (gsettings set … scaling-factor 0) is gone. A scale that cannot be read (−1) is declared and the session proceeds.

    The bus connection belongs to the MutterSession and is lent out by mutter_bus(): the clipboard uses the same RemoteDesktop session, because a second connection would be a second sender that Mutter does not recognise as the owner. The input channel opened here with ConnectToEIS and its recovery mutter_eis_reattach() are described in ch. 10 “Input”.

    6.4 · KDE: the KWin screencast protocol and the nested KWin

    On Plasma the capture is a Wayland request to KWin: the private protocol zkde_screencast_unstable_v1, asked for KWin's only output, answers with the id of a PipeWire node. From the node on, the path is the GNOME one: capture_start(node). On Kubuntu 26.04 KWin and Plasma are 6.6.7 (kwin-wayland, in Ubuntu's universe). The comments of kwin.c name KWin 6.3.6 for the oldest measurements (October 2026, a nested KWin in labwc 0.8.3) and KWin 6.6.6 and 6.6.7 for the ones taken on Ubuntu.

    The gate. KWin announces zkde_screencast_unstable_v1 only to a client whose executable (/proc/<pid>/exe, canonical) appears in the Exec= line of a .desktop file that lists the protocol in X-KDE-Wayland-Interfaces. The package installs that file as /usr/share/applications/org.kde.remotix.desktop (source debian/org.kde.remotix.desktop, Exec=/usr/libexec/remotix/remotix), and the server only verifies it at startup with kwin_check_permission() (file present, Exec= pointing to the running binary, protocol declared; the failure codes are RX-KDE-001, RX-KDE-002 and RX-KDE-003). The child is an execve of the same binary, so it is the process KWin recognises. KWin's environment also needs XDG_MENU_PREFIX=plasma-, or its service index is built empty (session.c).

    The size: KWin nested in labwc. KWin on a machine without a seat cannot use its DRM backend, and the comments of kwin.h record that, up to KWin 6.7, its --virtual backend can neither resize its output nor create another, while restarting KWin at a new size kills every program that is not Qt. Therefore KWin is born nested: session.c writes a drop-in for Plasma's plasma-kwin_wayland user unit whose ExecStart is remotix --kwin-nested W H NODE -- kwin_wayland_wrapper --xwayland --width W --height H --no-lockscreen. That mode of the same binary (kwin_nested_alive(), called from main.c) starts a labwc without a screen (WLR_BACKENDS=headless) in a runtime folder of its own, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/remotix-kwin-host, brings its output to W×H, and then becomes the KWin wrapper with --wayland-display added. KWin opens one full-screen window in labwc, and its output follows the size of that window. NODE is the render node chosen by card_pick_desktop() (ch. 7 “Video encoding”), pixman when no card can create a buffer, or - to let wlroots choose.

    The labwc is REMOTIX's own. The path is compiled in: src/Makefile passes -DREMOTIX_LABWC="/usr/libexec/remotix/labwc" (the make variable LABWC, which debian/rules sets to the same path), and kwin_nested_alive() runs the file at that path if access() finds it executable. It is not the distribution's labwc: the comments of kwin.c record that with KWin 6.5 and later the distribution's labwc leaves KWin on its first frame, because its wlroots never reports KWin's root surface as presented. The measurement of 18 Nov 2026 (studio/10-kde-controprova-labwc.md, Ubuntu's labwc against REMOTIX's, 30 s) counted the wp_presentation_feedback answers: 0 presented and 755 discarded with the distribution's labwc, 759 presented and 1 discarded with REMOTIX's. In the first case the clients get frame callbacks with time 0 and Firefox stops painting (9 intervals out of 11 without a changed pixel). The programs of the session are not affected otherwise: a terminal still updates in both cases, which is why a first test misled.

    The binary comes from build/labwc-ospite/: VERSIONS pins labwc 0.9.3 and wlroots 0.19.2 with their sha256, fetch.sh downloads and verifies the two archives, build.sh applies the patch wlroots-0.19.2-remotix-presented-root.patch (a few lines in wlroots' types/scene/surface.c, so that the root surface is reported as presented), builds with meson with only the GLES2 and pixman renderers (-Dwlroots:renderers=gles2) and fails if the result links a shared libwlroots. wlroots is linked statically, so the program does not depend on the distribution's wlroots. It exists only for KDE: XFCE and LXQt keep using the distribution's labwc. Licensing: labwc is GPL-2.0, wlroots is MIT, and the corresponding source of the shipped binary is published with each release as an archive named remotix-<version>-labwc-source.tar.gz (ch. 15 “The package”). That the shipped binary is the one installed was checked on Kubuntu by comparing the sha256 (round 2, K5).

    Reattach at another size. The child dismantles the stage first, because KWin's stream would otherwise renegotiate to a size the fixed offer refuses and die, then changes labwc's output with kwin_host_resize() (the zwlr_output_manager_v1 road of XFCE and LXQt), waits up to 3 s for KWin's own output to read the new size, and remounts the stage. Before mounting, kwin_host_settle() (3 s) waits until KWin's output has the size the host was asked for, because the comments record that at birth labwc configures KWin's window more than once and that a capture mounted in between offers a size the stream no longer has (those timings are from KWin 6.3.6 and labwc 0.8.3). On Kubuntu the reattach checks are green in the round of 18 Nov 2026 (desktop/reattach-windows-inside). The programs of the session stay.

    The ScreenSaver sidecar. screensaver_alive() in kwin.c is a process of its own, forked like the ticker, that owns the name org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver on both object paths in use (/ScreenSaver and /org/freedesktop/ScreenSaver) and never locks anything. GetActive, the time queries and SimulateUserActivity get a harmless answer; Lock, Throttle and UnThrottle get the standard error NotSupported; Inhibit is forwarded to the same powerdevil call the application would have made, with the same arguments and cookie, and given back when the caller leaves the bus or calls UnInhibit (measured with VLC: with the name present VLC asks the ScreenSaver first and would not go on after an error). The name is asked for with DO_NOT_QUEUE: if a real owner is ever there first, the sidecar ends and says so. It dies with the unit's cgroup at the end of the session and writes nothing in the user's files. Measured with a stand-in on Plasma 6.6.7 on 18 Nov 2026: the logout prompt appears within 1 s. The sidecar entered the package unione3 (19 Nov 2026), and from that round on input-chrome/page-cad-chain and input-firefox/page-cad-chain are green on Kubuntu (the earlier red lines of 18 Nov are the defect it cures); in the round of unione5 every line of the Kubuntu box is green (docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md).

    Without our labwc. When REMOTIX_LABWC is not executable, kwin_nested_alive() execs KWin with --virtual and prints a declared fallback («our labwc is not installed»); it never falls back to the distribution's labwc, which would reproduce the defect above. The output keeps the size it was born with, stage_size() captures the size KWin reports (kwin_measure()), and a reattach at another size no longer changes the desktop. kwin_host_exists() is how the child tells the two cases apart.

    The «unchanged» filter. The header unchanged.h records that KWin delivered about 50 buffers a second for five real changes (3776×2016, Firefox client), roughly 45 of them the same picture. A KWin frame whose damaged rectangles hold the same bytes as the last frame that went out is not encoded. The filter is switched on by capture_skip_unchanged(), which child.c calls only for KWin, and it is ignored on a wlroots capture. Its limits, all constants of unchanged.h:

    Empty damage. KWin 6.6 is recorded as sending about 60 frames a second even on a still screen, with SPA_META_VideoDamage present and empty for the ones that changed nothing. damage_classify() counts them in empty_damage and the buffer goes back to PipeWire without being encoded; the frame is never skipped right after the start, after a renegotiated format or a resize, or when its damage was lost (deliver_next, damage_lost). The comment of capture.c (28 Oct 2026) records that, counted as «absent», those 53 frames a second of nothing were encoded and the client fell 1–3 s behind. The comment of capture.h (19 Nov 2026, KWin 6.6.7) adds that a poke on a still desktop (next section) is answered with one whole frame whose damage is empty: 68 pokes gave 68 such frames, all dropped.

    The cursor. KWin is asked for cursor metadata (mode 4), which makes every pointer movement produce a buffer without new pixels marked SPA_CHUNK_FLAG_CORRUPTED; capture.c discards those and counts them in cursor_only. KWin draws the pointer into the image, so the session runs with REMOTIX's encoded cursor theme (6.11 “The encoded cursor theme”), and the child calls capture_cursor_never_hide() so that an empty metadata image is never forwarded as «hidden». The declared price: on Plasma an application that hides the pointer does not hide it for the viewer.

    6.5 · The lost frame (KWin)

    On Kubuntu 26.04 (KWin 6.6.7, PipeWire 1.6.2) a window that had just been opened could stay in the browser half way through its opening animation, translucent and smaller, for 18 to 26 s, while KWin's own output showed the whole window from the first second. The cause is a buffer that KWin queued and PipeWire never delivered to REMOTIX. The cure is in capture.c, child.c and kwin.c. The reasoning and the measurements are recorded only in the comments of the code (the end of capture.h, the head of capture.c, the call sites in child.c); this section is their documentation. It is not described in DECISIONS.md or in the register of problems.

    What was measured

    KWin numbers every buffer it queues in the seq field of spa_meta_header, cursor-only buffers included. In every stalled run the numbers that reached on_process had holes: 198, 200, 202, 204, all cursor-only buffers, and never 199, 201, 203, which were the pictures. The comments mark this as measured (19 Nov 2026), and the explanation below as read in the sources of KWin 6.6.7 and PipeWire ([R] in the comments), not reproduced in isolation.

    Why the buffers are lost

    • Two buffers come close together. In KWin's screencaststream.cpp the record timer runs record(m_pendingContents) and then clears the pending contents. While record() draws, an effect that is still animating schedules the next repaint, which calls scheduleRecord() again from inside record(): the timer is started at 0 ms and the line after record() wipes what was asked. The timer fires with nothing to record, which with the cursor as metadata is a cursor-only buffer. During an animation every picture is followed, some tens of microseconds later, by a cursor-only buffer.
    • The first of the two is overwritten. KWin's stream is the driver of the PipeWire graph and every pw_stream_queue_buffer() starts a cycle. A cycle hands the buffer over by plain assignment (tee_process() in impl-port.c), and a cycle started before the reader has run for the previous one is started all the same (node_ready() in impl-node.c): the buffer not yet read is overwritten. PipeWire calls it an xrun; for a video stream it is a frame gone. REMOTIX's reader is a real-time callback that returns in microseconds, but it must be woken first, and on a busy machine (a session just born) it wakes after the second cycle.
    • Nothing to tune on the REMOTIX side. The number of buffers and the frame rate do not enter; the transport that waits for the reader (node.reliable, PipeWire 1.6) is chosen by the producer.

    What a lost picture costs

    Its damage is lost with it: the next picture declares only what changed after it, so part of the screen stays old. If it was the last picture of an animation nothing comes after it, and the stream stands at the previous frame until something else on the desktop changes. A pointer movement does not help, because it brings a cursor-only buffer.

    The cure, in two halves

    i
    Safety switch. the count rests on «one number per buffer». A producer that counted otherwise would show a hole at every buffer and every frame would go out as «all changed» with nobody told. If holes are seen in more than half of SEQ_WINDOW = 600 buffers (a window of 600, checked at its end), the count is switched off for that capture and the log says so. Measured on KWin 6.6.7: at most 30 holes in the roughly 200 buffers of a session being born. The mechanism never runs on a still desktop, because it needs a hole in the numbers to start.

    What the log says

    • «the buffers' numbers are watched: a hole in them is a buffer that never arrived…» (area capture) when the count is switched on;
    • «a buffer of KWin never arrived and no picture came after it: pixel on top committed again to have one drawn (so far: N holes in the numbers, N buffers missing, N pokes)», at most once a second;
    • «a buffer of KWin never arrived, and the pixel on top could NOT be committed again (no pixel, or no connection to KWin)», once until a poke succeeds again;
    • «N pokes in a row and no picture from KWin: I stop asking until one arrives by itself»;
    • «N holes in the numbers of the last 600 buffers … The count is switched OFF for this capture».

    What was verified, and what was not

    Measured: the holes in the numbers, the 68 pokes on a still desktop answered by 68 frames with empty damage, and the bound of 30 holes per ~200 buffers at session birth (all in the comments, 19 Nov 2026). The cure was approved by the reviewer on 19 Nov and is inside the package unione5, whose full round on the Kubuntu box is green on every line; the owner's hand tests of 19 Nov (the container machines with unione5, then the virtual machines and the live image with unione10) found Kubuntu regular. Not verified: the mechanism on a machine with a real GPU and a real seat (the measurements are from the test environment), the frequency of the defect after the cure, and PipeWire releases other than 1.6.2.

    6.6 · PipeWire negotiation, resize and wake-up

    On GNOME and KDE the capture is a PipeWire consumer created by capture_start() on the node the compositor announced. Everything is declared in the format proposal (proposal()) and in the consumption parameters (consumer_parameters()).

    i
    The card that refuses linear. when the card refuses a linear render buffer (the comments record NVIDIA with GNOME 50 on Ubuntu 26.04, measured on 6 Oct 2026 with an earlier version of the code; not run again on this tree, and whether Intel or the Radeon negotiate DMA-BUF modifiers like that card is not verified), the proposal LINEAR + INVALID ended in «no more input formats». modifiers_per_route() in child.c asks vulkanvideo_card_rejects_linear() and only then passes the modifiers the Vulkan encoder can import to capture_modifiers_card()

    Buffer generation. Every time PipeWire reallocates its buffers (renegotiation, wake-up) on_buffer_added() and on_buffer_removed() change a generation counter that travels with every frame (generation). The encoder caches the import of each DMA-BUF, and file descriptor numbers are recycled: a cache keyed on the descriptor alone would hand the encoder a surface pointing to a freed buffer, an old image with no error. When the generation changes the cache is dropped.

    Retention. On the GPU path the pw_buffer is held until capture_stopped_free(), which the child calls only after the encoder call has returned, that is after the GPU has finished reading and not after the work was queued. Releasing earlier is the defect recorded in LESSONS.md §8 (two screens alternating, no error). release_held_buffer() gives the buffer back only if its generation is still current.

    What Mutter 50 changes

    Read in the source of Mutter 50.1 and not measured by hand (the effect is verified only through the rounds, where desktop/canvas-limits and media pass on GNOME 50.1): (1) the virtual stream is created with must-drive false and a passive frame clock (node.supports-request = 2); REMOTIX's consumer is a plain pw_stream and never the driver, so Mutter stays the driver as in earlier versions. (2) After every monitors-changed Mutter publishes the format parameters again, so a resize costs one more renegotiation, capture.c handles format changes already through the buffer generation. (3) The buffer range is 2 to 8 (it was 2 to 16); REMOTIX asks for 6 on the GPU path (minimum 4, maximum 8, capture.c) and 4 on the memory path, inside the range but with a narrower margin while the encoder retains two buffers. (4) Every format carries colorPrimaries = BT709 and transferFunction = GAMMA22 as non-mandatory properties, and Mutter 50 composes SDR with gamma 2.2; colors709.c uses the BT.709 matrix and ignores the transfer tag (7.8 “BT.709 colour conversion”). No comparison of images between Debian and Ubuntu was made.

    Resizing a live stream

    capture_resize() rebuilds the proposal at the new size and calls pw_stream_update_params(), without touching the session or the virtual monitor. It returns CAPTURE_RECANVAS_REQUESTED, CAPTURE_RECANVAS_UNCHANGED (the size is already in force: renegotiating it would chase its own tail) or CAPTURE_RECANVAS_FAULT. «Requested» is not «done»: the next frame at the new size is the witness. The comments record that a size the producer cannot hold kills the stream about 2 ms later («no more input formats»); capture_take() looks at the state before waiting, so the failure surfaces in one loop turn instead of a timeout. The size rule itself (RCP_CANVAS_MIN_W 320 to RCP_CANVAS_MAX_W 4096, RCP_CANVAS_MIN_H 240 to RCP_CANVAS_MAX_H 2304, even sides, larger requests reduced; the declared limit of the product is 3K) lives in rcp_size_allowed() (ch. 5 “The RCP/1 protocol”).

    Waking a still desktop

    A Wayland compositor delivers only when the scene changes, and a desktop just started is still. Wayland has no «repaint now», but restarting the stream makes a buffer arrive. capture_wake() repeats the current parameters at the negotiated size; on labwc it asks for the next frame whole (wlr_force_full()). The child calls it only when a keyframe is owed and the capture returned zero, and at most every WAKEUP_MS = 400 ms.

    !
    Wake-up and held buttons. on Mutter the renegotiation recreates the absolute input devices (the comment of capture.h traces it to viewports-changed and remove_viewport_devices(), which does not go through drop_device()). If a button is held at that moment it stays pressed inside Mutter and the desktop would take no other click. The child therefore does not wake the stream while input_pressed() reports a key or button held; the price is that a client just attached may see a blank page until the user lets go. input.c has a further healing for the doors the child does not control (ch. 10 “Input”). The chain was measured on Mutter 48.7 (Debian). In the source of Mutter 50.1 drop_device() and handle_button() are unchanged, but the cure was not measured again on Ubuntu: the bench that measured it is not in this tree.

    When the compositor refuses the GPU path. A machine without 3D acceleration has no DMA-BUF to offer, and the GPU proposal dies with «no more input formats». capture_format_refused() recognises the facts (stream in error with no format ever agreed, or a format agreed and no frame ever delivered) and capture_start() returns G_IO_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED when it sees the refusal itself. falls_back_if_refused() in the child then switches to memory, logs it, and never tries the GPU again in that process. The two paths are never offered together, because the compositor would choose and zero copy would be lost where it works. Silence (no frame in 5 s) does not trigger the fallback; only a refusal does. Since 17 Nov 2026 the package refuses a new installation on a machine with no DRM render node at all (ch. 15 “The package”), so this fallback is the safety net for a card that exists but gives no DMA-BUF.

    Closing the stage. pw_stream_destroy() when the stage is dismantled can wait for RealtimeKit for up to 25 s on a machine where rtkit-daemon is installed but does not start: the real-time module of the two PipeWire contexts (capture.c, sound.c) stays in a D-Bus call. For that reason the child announces the end of a session before the stage is dismantled (3.10 “When the session ends before the stage is gone”).

    6.7 · XFCE and LXQt: wlroots screencopy

    labwc has no PipeWire node. It offers zwlr_screencopy_manager_v1 (version 3), and every frame is a full round trip: capture_output, buffer, copy, ready. The frame rate is therefore REMOTIX's loop, not a property of the compositor.

    Why a separate module. capture.c was built on the push direction and child.c uses its interface in dozens of places; the comment of capture.h counts thirty-five. Rewriting them for two directions would have put GNOME and KDE at risk to serve a new desktop. The shape copies the clipboard's precedent (clipboard_open() and clipboard_open_kde()): a second constructor, capture_start_wlr(), and every public function of capture.c hands over to wlroots.c at the top when the capture is a wlroots one. Everything downstream (capture_take(), capture_delivery(), the counters) sees no difference.

    The environment in which this compositor is born is set by session.c: WLR_BACKENDS=headless (no seat and no libseat), WLR_LIBINPUT_NO_DEVICES=1, LABWC_UPDATE_ACTIVATION_ENV=1 (without it labwc does not propagate WAYLAND_DISPLAY to the bus), and WLR_RENDER_DRM_DEVICE with the node chosen by card_pick_desktop(), or WLR_RENDERER=pixman as a declared fallback when no card can create the output buffer (ch. 7 “Video encoding”).

    6.8 · Slabs: zero copy on labwc

    On labwc the zero-copy path is a copy into a DMA-BUF that REMOTIX owns. A «slab» is a GBM buffer allocated on the compositor's render node, its DMA-BUF descriptor and the wl_buffer that names it. wlr_ask_card() enables the path and says no in writing if it cannot, leaving memory as a declared fallback. The module chose it over zwlr_export_dmabuf_manager_v1 because the exported buffers belong to the compositor's swap chain, are reused every turn and are always marked transient, with no lever at all on reuse; a buffer of REMOTIX's own costs one blit on the GPU and one dependency, gbm.

    • Three slabs (WLR_SLABS): one in hand, one in flight, one as insurance. If all are in hand the frame stops and says so; a slab in hand is never recycled, and wlr_release() is called from capture_stopped_free(), after the encoder has finished reading.
    • Linear modifier. The linux_dmabuf event carries format and size, not modifiers, so slabs are LINEAR. The exception is a card whose GBM refuses linear rendering buffers: the slab is then allocated with one of the modifiers the Vulkan encoder imports (vulkanvideo_modifiers()).
    • Exact format. The slab is allocated in exactly the format and size of the linux_dmabuf event; anything else is invalid buffer, a protocol error that kills the connection.
    • Synchronisation. The comments record that wlroots ends the blit with glFlush() and sends ready at once, and that labwc offers no explicit-sync protocol. After ready REMOTIX extracts the fence from the DMA-BUF (DMA_BUF_IOCTL_EXPORT_SYNC_FILE with DMA_BUF_SYNC_READ) and polls it; the wait is gpu_wait_us. Without the ioctl it is said once and implicit synchronisation is trusted.
    • Generation. Every slab that is born or dies changes the generation, for the same descriptor-reuse reason as on PipeWire.
    • Switching off. WLR_CARD_FAILED_MAX = 3 consecutive failed on the GPU path turn it off, and the log says so; the first slab birth may take up to WLR_SLAB_BIRTH_S = 1 s.
    !
    Slabs and the AMD GPU hang. when the encoder is Vulkan, slabs_per_route() calls wlr_slabs_at_max_canvas() and the slabs are born at WLR_SLAB_W × WLR_SLAB_H = 4096×2304 (the largest canvas, RCP_CANVAS_MAX_W × RCP_CANVAS_MAX_H), and a resize changes only the wl_buffer, never the GBM object. The comment of wlroots.c explains why: GBM (radeonsi) and Vulkan (RADV) in the same process share one amdgpu_device, and freeing a GBM buffer right before creating the Vulkan encoder at the new size is recorded as a page fault, VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST and a card reset (10 faults in 14 runs with slabs freed on resize, 0 in 5 with slabs kept, on an AMD card; measured on an earlier build, never re-measured on Ubuntu). The cost is 3 × 4096 × 2304 × 4 = about 113 MB per session even at 1080p, so it applies only to the Vulkan route. With VA-API the slabs keep the canvas size. Which route a Radeon takes on Ubuntu 26.04 is in 7.3 “Choosing the GPU route”.

    6.9 · Zero copy and the memory fallback

    «Zero copy» means the frame never leaves the GPU between the compositor and the encoder. It is the default: ZERO_COPY is 1 in child.c, and a compile-time -DZERO_COPY=0 exists only to rebuild the «before» for A/B comparisons. It is not zero work: the RGB to YUV conversion still happens, on the GPU.

    The 64-byte stride. CARD_ALIGNMENT in encoder.c is 64 bytes. The comments record that the Intel iHD driver, importing a DMA-BUF whose stride is not a multiple of 64, reads rows at its own pitch and the desktop comes out blurred and slanted while the timing looks perfect, with no error. The producer makes the stride equal to width × 4, so the code refuses the GPU path for such a canvas and declares it, rather than sending a wrong image.

    Remounting only the capture. Switching path does not tear down the stage. remount_only_capture() stops and reopens only the Capture and its cursor hook, keeping the input channel, the clipboard and the RemoteDesktop session; the comments record a crash inside ei_disconnect() after a full teardown shortly after the EIS channel was opened. On labwc the capture is the source, so remounting means capture_stop() and capture_start_wlr().

    i
    One frame rate, short waits. the frame rate is one number, MOTION_FPS = 60, used both for the capture maximum and for the encoder. The child waits MOTION_WAIT_S = 8 ms per turn, so that on a still desktop a click does not wait in the socket for a long poll.

    6.10 · The cursor channel

    The pointer is drawn by the page, not baked into the video: the image stays clean (two pointers are worse than one) and the shape travels as a side channel, the CURSOR_SHAPE message of RCP/1. The capture's only addition to its interface is the registration of the receiver (the seam is described at the end of capture.h); cursor.c sits between the capture and the wire. The shape is delivered from the capture, on the real-time thread for the PipeWire desktops.

    After a hidden period Mutter sends «unchanged» when the pointer comes back, so cursor.c keeps the last visible shape and re-sends it; otherwise the pointer would stay invisible with no error. A cursor larger than 256 would make the receiver close the session with a protocol error, which is why the limit is enforced on this side. A malformed metadata block is declared in the log (malformed_cursors) and nothing is sent.

    6.11 · The encoded cursor theme

    KWin and labwc draw the pointer into the captured image, so their sessions run with a cursor theme of REMOTIX's own, SHAPE_THEME = remotix-invisible. Each shape of that theme is a 1×1 image, opaque and of a colour that is its alone. The server writes the theme before the desktop starts (shape_theme_write() is called from session.c); the child reads the colour and looks up the real image in a real theme on disk. The design is an encoded theme plus a dictionary (shape.h, shape.c).

    The labwc probe. wlr_probe_pointer() runs a capture_output_region of 3×3 pixels around the hotspot into a small wl_shm buffer; the centre is checked, then the neighbours. Only one probe is in flight, coalescing to the last position; it is a plain copy, never with damage; and a tail probe PROBE_TAIL_US = 120 ms after the hand stops catches the shape change a client makes after the enter event. MIN_PROBE_US is 0: probes are not thinned.

    !
    The declared price. the compositor now paints one coloured pixel under the hotspot into the image. The browser's pointer covers it and the encoder smears it; the header of shape.h marks «never visible» as not settled until someone looks, and nobody has looked by eye. The pointer-shape-* checks pass on the four desktops in the Ubuntu rounds. Which real theme is found on Xubuntu and Lubuntu depends on the themes installed (REAL_THEMES lists Adwaita then breeze_cursors): not verified.

    6.12 · Capture constants and what was verified

    The constants of the capture, where they live.

    Every capture line in the log carries the area capture, also those written by kwin.c, mutter.c and wlroots.c. The line written when the stage is mounted names the route (CARD or MEMORY), because the timings of the two are not the same quantity (ch. 16 “Logging and diagnostics”).

    What was verified, and what was not

    • The round of 26-27 Nov 2026 ran prove/all.sh on the four desktops, each in its own virtual machine with the Radeon handed over (RX_BANCO=vm), with Chrome and Firefox: GNOME 125 PASS and one known FAIL, KDE, XFCE and LXQt 126 PASS. The cures described in this chapter (the early farewell of the session, the ScreenSaver sidecar, the lost-frame cure, the GNOME scale cure) were made in the rounds of 18 and 19 Nov 2026, before 1.0.1 (docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md).
