The two deny unix lines of the profile say the same of abstract sockets, and unlike the rest of the profile they hold even in complain mode. On the real live Kubuntu, with the Radeon driven by VA-API, the same line reads HEVC: yes via vaapi where the virtual machines read yes via vulkan (docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md, 19 Nov 2026: the two encoding roads were both exercised, on different benches).

    The session's dconf (D-015)

    Ubuntu's GNOME needs the rules of the remote session (no lock, no user switching, the integer scale 1, Log Out kept, the keyboard layout) to be read by every program of the session, including the snap and Flutter programs that read dconf through their own reader. The model is a runtime profile $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/dconf/profile with the layers system-db:remotix (/etc/dconf/db/remotix: the locks and values, made by the package) and user-db:remotix (~/.config/dconf/remotix: the three keys that change during the session), on top of the user's own base profile. Its lines are in the session area; the decision is called D-015 in the code and in the register of problems (C5). The caption of the table says which lines come from recorded runs and which only from the code.

    Other lines new in this tree

    While running, the parent writes once a minute a cumulative line about the local-session guardian (guardian: calls=… worst_ms=… tenants=… loop_gaps=… worst_gap_ms=…, period GUARDIAN_COUNT_MS = 60,000 ms) instead of one line per two-second pass. At shutdown it sends the farewell RCP_SERVER_CLOSING to every session and reports how many sessions did not finish within the wait (main.c).

    16.10 · Lines of the stop, the orphan rule and the local-login hold

    The lines below are those of the stop of the service (3.11 “Stopping the service”), of the rule “no orphan desktops” and of the local-login hold (14.6 “The local-login hold”). The text is that of the code; N stands for a number, and long lines are cut with “…”. Follow them with journalctl -t remotix | grep 'local login' or journalctl -t remotix | grep -E 'no orphan|stopping'.

    A request whose user has no REMOTIX desktop leaves only a detail line (local login of uid N: no REMOTIX desktop of that user — the login goes on, --verbose). What the page of a client that is refused a birth during the hold shows was not traced for this manual.

    16.11 · Environment variables read by the product

    REMOTIX reads almost nothing from the environment, on purpose. The complete list of names that start with REMOTIX_ in src/ and debian/, leaving out the include guards of the headers (REMOTIX_*_H), is in the table. Three are read with getenv() by the product; two are service variables read by systemd; two are journal fields, not variables. Other occurrences of the prefix are not variables either: REMOTIX_BENCH is a compile-time define (make BENCH=1), REMOTIX_LABWC is a compile-time define too (the path of the package's own labwc, /usr/libexec/remotix/labwc by default, set by LABWC= in src/Makefile and read by kwin.c; 15.6 “Our own labwc (KDE)”), REMOTIX_SPLIT and REMOTIX_SGOMBRA_SOGLIA_MS survive only in comments, and the REMOTIX_* names in page.html are JavaScript objects.

    The administrator sets the two service variables in /etc/remotix/remotix.conf.d/*.conf, which the unit reads after the defaults in /usr/share/remotix/remotix.conf (EnvironmentFile lines in debian/remotix.service); a later file wins.

    !
    Which processes see these variables. REMOTIX_VPP_PADDING and REMOTIX_VULKAN_CONVERSION are read where the encoder opens. The encoder of a real session runs in the per-user child, whose environment become_and_exec() builds from scratch (HOME, USER, LOGNAME, PATH, SHELL, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, the bus address, and XDG_SESSION_ID from PAM). Neither variable reaches a real session. They reach the startup probe (a fork of the parent) and the command remotix --encoding-test, which is how the benches use them. rootside.c (net_environment()) does pass every REMOTIX_ variable of the root side to the network side, but the network side does not read any of them today.

    Other variables the code reads are the standard ones of the session it lives in: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, WAYLAND_DISPLAY, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, XDG_STATE_HOME (through GLib, for the session log), XDG_DATA_HOME and HOME (session.c: where the user's data folder is, for the session's own files), DCONF_PROFILE, LANG, PATH, USER and JOURNAL_STREAM (log.c, session.c, kwin.c, wlroots.c, wlr_input.c, child.c). DCONF_PROFILE is read, not given: in the runtime model of D-015 the session gets no DCONF_PROFILE (its profile is the file $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/dconf/profile), and a value that the administrator put in the user manager's environment is taken as the base profile and said in a line of the session area; only the declared fallback sets it for the session. Variables used only by the test scripts are in ch. 17 “Testing”.

    16.12 · Diagnostic instruments

    Besides the log, the product carries a few instruments for diagnosis. None is on in the packaged service except --journal: the unit's ExecStart carries no bench option, and BENCH_ON is 0 in rcp.c.

    One more mode of the binary is not an instrument but is easy to meet in the sources: remotix --dconf-keyfiles DIR (answered by main() before any other option) writes the two keyfiles of the GNOME session's dconf rules into DIR from the one table the program uses (DCONF_KEYS in session.c). It is run by debian/rules at build time and by nobody afterwards; it opens nothing else and exits 0 or 1.

    The diagnostics mode of the page

    The page keeps a text log of its own decisions and counters in the element #logbook (the function note() in page.html appends to it). Since 16 Aug 2026 it is hidden by default: the style rule body:not(.diagnostics) #logbook hides it, and with it the small keyboard-shortcut button and its notice, which sat where users reach for the desktop's own controls. The text still accumulates in the DOM, so diagnostics do not depend on having been visible. It appears with ?logbook in the address, or from the browser console with REMOTIX.logbook(true) (logbook_visible()); REMOTIX.logbook(false) hides it again. The same window.REMOTIX object exposes viewer, version and the counters that the benches read; the comment in page.html calls it an object to read, not a switch that changes the page's behaviour. The array SC_LOG (at most SC_LOG_MAX = 256 entries, exposed as REMOTIX.shortcuts.logbook) keeps the notes of the keyboard-shortcut engine for the benches. The page's other query options (?video=…, ?canvas=…, ?draw=mse, ?layout=…) are described in ch. 9 “The browser page”.

    !
    A test hook behind the diagnostics switch. ?logbook also arms a test-only hook: with it in the address, the fragment #video_fault=die|mute|blind makes the video worker misbehave on purpose, to prove the fallback on a test machine. It is read only from the fragment (which never reaches the server) and only together with ?logbook, so a link without it cannot break anybody's video.

    Reading a defect report

    1. Read the startup declarations (16.9 “The startup declarations”): most «it does not work» cases are already named there: no codec offered, no PAM service file, the KWin permission missing.
    2. Filter by user (REMOTIX_TENANT or the bracket) and by area; read budget for refusals, rcp for the handshake, session and child for the birth and the end of the desktop.
    3. For a refused login, tell PAM REFUSED (a real no) from ⛔ PAM COULD NOT JUDGE (a missing /etc/pam.d/remotix or a missing list file).
    4. For a desktop that is born and shows nothing, read the session lines and the user's session.log.
    5. Only then switch on --verbose, for the shortest time that reproduces the defect.
    +
    No silent exits. a session that disappears leaves a line with the numbers it was closed on (the dead-line values, the clock that expired, the farewell code). A disappearance without such a line is a defect of REMOTIX by the project's own invariant I1.
    Chapter 17

    Testing

    17.1 · What a check is and how it decides

    The tests of REMOTIX are not unit tests of C functions: the tree has no unit-test target, and src/Makefile builds the product only. Every check in prove/ works on one of the four virtual machines of the bench (17.8 “The VM bench”) with the package installed: it drives a real browser against it the way a person would (real mouse, keyboard and touch events through the browser's debugging interface), and decides its verdict from what happened inside the machine: a window in the user's session that writes down every event it receives, the journal, logind, the process list.

    Rules that hold for every check, taken from the docstrings of prove/lib.py and of the check files:

    • Three verdicts, one line each. A check prints PASS name - evidence, FAIL name - evidence or BLOCKED name - evidence, and exits 0 only if every named check is PASS. FAIL means the product did not do it (this includes: the page does not answer, a valid login is refused). BLOCKED means the tool could not look (the browser did not start, Marionette did not answer, an earlier step broke). The Results class of prove/lib.py enforces it: a broken tool step is BLOCKED, never a PASS. all.sh adds two kinds of row that are not verdicts, SKIP (reason) and NOTE (17.4 “Running the suite”).
    • Nothing is shared between runs. Each run starts its own headless labwc in its own runtime directory (class Compositor, started in a private user, network and mount namespace so that it takes none of the host's X display numbers), its own browser profile, and DevTools or Marionette ports picked by the operating system. On the VM bench the Radeon is handed to one machine at a time, so the desktops are tried one after the other.
    • Every wait has a deadline. guard() sets a whole-run alarm; every failure of the tool is a ToolError that says why. The compositor and the browsers are children of the check and die with it. The environment variable RX_TEMPO (an integer of at least 1, anything else is refused, never read as «no deadline») multiplies every deadline: the VM bench runs with 2 (all.sh sets it).
    • The users are the check's own. Each check creates users with a prefix of its own (bc, lc, mu, rs, ac, cb, bn, dk, dkf, md, in, ph, pl, followed by digits; check-package.py uses pkg and a desktop prefix), and sweep() at the end of all.sh ends every session of the thirteen prefixes just listed (the pattern is the same in lib.py and in prove/banco-vm/fresh-vm.sh, which also deletes the users). The checks that are not in all.sh use the prefix kx (check-exit.py, check-kde-exit.py), which the pattern does not contain: the check removes its own user. A login with a user that may not exist is never tried, because a wrong login counts for the address ban (ch. 13 “Login and its defences”).
    • Verdicts are built on the application, not on what the browser was told. A key counts as delivered only when window-input.py inside the session logged it.
    i
    Where they run. The checks run on the dev server only. They need QEMU with OVMF and the vfio set-up (the VM bench), the host's PipeWire-pulse for Firefox audio, two browsers, labwc and PIL; server/prepara-server-vm.sh installs them after every reboot (the server's root file system is in RAM; no podman and no container). There are no containers on the bench: tests and studies run on virtual machines.

    Nothing in this chapter was run while writing the manual. The results quoted in 17.12 “What was verified on Ubuntu 26.04, and what was not” are the recorded logs of the dev server and the notes of docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md and of the register of problems.

    17.2 · The files of prove/

    Everything is under prove/. The Python files form three layers: libraries, checks, and test windows that run inside the virtual machine.

    The folders shots/ (pictures), work/ and log/ are made by the checks and are not in git; the logs quoted in this manual are on the dev server, in /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove/log/ (one folder per round, named by its tag).

    17.3 · The checks of all.sh and what each proves

    All checks take --box xfce|lxqt|gnome|kde (REMOTIX ports 8841 to 8844 on the virtual machines, see 17.8 “The VM bench”). The limits are the seconds given to each run call in all.sh; the verdict names are the NAMES tuples of each file. The list is that of the tree when this chapter was written (20 Nov 2026): check-desktop.py was being edited at that moment, and the two last names of its tuple, power-implied and power-local-seat, are of 20 Nov 2026.

    In the tree the tuples give, per desktop and with the default all.sh (prelocal P1 to P6), 126 verdict rows: base 5 and 5, lifecycle 4, multiuser 3, desktop 9, media 4, resilience 5, audio 1 and 1, clipboard 2, input 26 with Chrome and 27 with Firefox, phone 19, prelocal 6, ban 8 (the seven names and cleanup), apparmor 1. The rounds of 1.2.0 on the four machines are in 17.12 “What was verified on Ubuntu 26.04, and what was not”.

    The two checks added on 20 November 2026

    power-implied needs no session and no Python in the box. It reads the installed rule 50-remotix-no-poweroff.rules and every polkit policy file of the machine, builds the implications (the annotation org.freedesktop.policykit.imply, followed along chains) and fails if an action that the rule does not forbid implies one that it forbids: polkit would then grant the forbidden action without consulting the rule. power-local-seat runs from root with no REMOTIX session and asks pkcheck, as the process of the greeter (the active session on seat0, that is the person at the machine), about every forbidden action: all must be refused. It is calibrated against login1.chvt, which must be granted; with no greeter (a container) it is BLOCKED. They exist because power-entries-absent looked only from the remote session, which is not at a seat, and only at the 15 actions known by name (register of problems, C6: the four set-reboot-* actions imply reboot).

    Both were run on the Ubuntu GNOME virtual machine on 20 Nov 2026, first with the rule of 15 actions of the package unione10 (run vm-gnome-poweroff-prima2/): both FAILED, as the register describes. power-implied named the four actions, set-reboot-parameter, set-reboot-to-boot-loader-entry, set-reboot-to-boot-loader-menu and set-reboot-to-firmware-setup, each implying login1.reboot; power-local-seat said «from the seat's active session c1 (leader 1846) polkit GRANTS: reboot». The same run had power-entries-absent PASS with «polkit refuses 15/15 power actions». Then with the rule of 19 actions (package unione11; run vm-gnome-poweroff-dopo/): power-implied PASS («19 forbidden actions … 51 policy files read; no action left alone implies a forbidden one») and power-local-seat PASS («from the active session of seat0 (c1, process 1846) all 19 forbidden actions are refused; calibration: chvt granted»). Limit: that run is a partial round of the desktop check alone (its summary.txt says «PARTIAL RUN, only: desktop»: 8 PASS and 1 FAIL, the known users-shell-and-environment); the complete round of 120/2/1/3 belongs to unione10 and was not repeated on unione11.

    Things to know before reading a log

    • check-ban.py is the only check that types wrong passwords, and it bans the address the browser comes from on that box: 127.0.0.1 on the containers, 10.0.2.2 on the VM bench (QEMU's user network shows every client as that address), or the value of RX_BAN_ADDR. To unblock it uses a drop-in with --command-socket (a bench option of the binary that the packaged unit never passes; the check adds it through REMOTIX_OPTIONS in /etc/remotix/remotix.conf.d/) and at the end it ALWAYS unblocks, removes the drop-in, restarts the service and logs a user in normally (cleanup). If the cleanup did not run, the check prints a NOTE that says what to undo by hand (on a VM: all.sh <de> --clean or banco-vm/fresh-vm.sh). Run it last and alone on a box.
    • check-prelocal.py simulates the local login: the boxes have no display manager running, so the hook is run as root inside the box by hand, with the environment pam_exec would give it (PAM_TYPE=open_session, XDG_SEAT=seat0, class user, type wayland), and no local session is registered in logind. It proves the hook and the root side's answer; it does not prove the interplay with the periodic sweeps, which only a real local login exercises (ch. 24 “Appendix C — Known issues and open points”). P1 to P6 are the same on the VMs, which do have a real display manager: all.sh calls the hook by hand there. The real local login is P7 to P9 (the automatic login of the display manager, restarted in the machine), which all.sh runs only with RX_LOCALE_VERO=1 and otherwise lists as a SKIP row, prelocal/real-login. The owner decided on 26 Nov 2026 that these cases are allowed on the Ubuntu bench with the Radeon passed through (the freezes of the server on Debian came from the old drivers of the Debian machines).
    • check-phone.py is an emulation, not a phone: Chrome with DevTools device emulation (412x915 CSS px, device scale 2, touch events with pointer type touch, a mobile user agent, Italian language). What it cannot prove is listed in 17.11 “What only a real machine or a real phone can prove”.
    • check-input.py states its limits in its header: DevTools and WebDriver cannot press AltGr, so the Italian AltGr characters are sent as the character itself, which exercises the page's LETTER path; the browser's pointer lock and the operating system's own cursor are in no screenshot, so the cursor is judged by the CSS rule on the canvas.
    • check-desktop.py on Ubuntu 26.04: the GNOME terminal is ptyxis (not gnome-terminal); sudo is sudo-rs, so a refusal is recognised also by «I'm afraid I can't do that» and «interactive authentication is required»; VOLATILE (the files that the desktop itself writes and that settings-intact does not count) now includes .config/dconf/remotix, the file that REMOTIX makes by design. session-cap needs a quiet box.
    • canvas-limits waits for the test window to say ready (up to 150 s; up to about 78 s was measured), waits for a picture that has stopped moving (still_png()), tries once more a picture that never stood still, and ignores a few stray pixels near the colour when it measures the window (the sky-blue launcher icon of KDE). The canvas it expects is the one of SPECS §6.1 (client area rounded down to 16, 320x240 to 4096x2304) limited by the maximum that the page itself declares (video.max_size MEASURED in the page's log, read by page_max_size()); the page declares at most 3840x2160 (the last rung of MEASURE_PROBES in page.html), and the evidence line says so: the server's bound of 4096x2304 cannot be exercised with this page. The declared limit of the product is 3K (owner's decision, DECISIONS-11 §11.51, confirmed 18 Nov 2026); the sizes above are technical bounds.
    • The check docstrings can lag behind the code: the docstring of check-ban.py still describes unblock-shipped as «the PACKAGE gives the administrator a way to unblock», while the code passes it when the package ships none. The code is the reference.

    17.4 · Running the suite

    A run is one command per desktop, started on the dev server in prove/. On the VM bench the machines run one at a time, because the Radeon is handed to one of them. On the older container boxes the four desktops could run at the same time: the runs share nothing (own compositor, browser profile and ports; each box has its own users and files).

    Running all.sh
    $ cd /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove
$ /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove/all.sh xfce                    # older container box: the package already installed in it
$ /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove/all.sh gnome --fresh /path/to/remotix_1.2.0-1+ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb     # container way
$ TAG=myround /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove/all.sh kde         # logs in log/myround/ instead of log/kde-<date>-<time>/
$ RX_BANCO=vm /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove/all.sh gnome --fresh <deb>   # the VM bench: the machine 'ubuntu', clean state, then the package
$ RX_BANCO=vm /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove/all.sh gnome --clean         # VM bench: clean state, the installed package stays
$ RX_BANCO=vm /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove/all.sh gnome --only ban,audio-firefox   # a partial round
$ RX_LOCALE_VERO=1 RX_BANCO=vm /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove/all.sh gnome --clean   # also P7, P8, P9 (the real local login)
    • --fresh <deb> first runs fresh.sh (container: reset the box, install the package, enable and start the service, check it is active; VM: the clean state of fresh-vm.sh, then the package); if that fails the run stops and every row is BLOCKED. --clean exists only with RX_BANCO=vm: the same clean-up with no package. Without --fresh or --clean nothing is cleaned, on a VM as on a container.
    • --only label,label runs a subset. The labels are base-chrome base-firefox lifecycle multiuser desktop media resilience audio-chrome audio-firefox clipboard input-chrome input-firefox phone prelocal ban apparmor package; an unknown label is refused with the list. package is a valid label but runs nothing: check-package.py is not part of all.sh (on a VM it is a SKIP row).
    • The output of each check goes to log/<tag>/<check>.out, ending with an exit=<n> line. Each verdict line becomes one table row <check>/<name>; a check that printed no verdict line is BLOCKED ("no verdict"), and one that hit its time limit is BLOCKED ("no answer").
    • After the last check lib.sweep() ends the sessions of the test users; a session left over is a BLOCKED row.
    • The table is printed and saved as log/<tag>/summary.txt. Besides the check rows it can hold NOTE rows (the bench key was installed in the VM; the Welcome Center of KDE was hidden in /etc/skel by the bench) and SKIP (reason) rows (never a PASS, never a failure). The last lines are lines of the checks: N PASS, N FAIL, N BLOCKED/other, N SKIP, N NOTE and one of: ALL PASS, ALL PASS (n SKIP with the reason in the table, none of them a PASS), ALL PASS OF A PARTIAL RUN (only: …): not a full run, NO CHECK PRODUCED A PASS: nothing proven (not ALL green), or «N line(s) not PASS».
    • Exit status. 0: a full run, every line PASS. 1: anything else, including an aborted run and a failed clean-up or initial control. 2: a wrong call (usage, unknown label, a bad RX_TEMPO). 3: every line PASS but the run was partial (--only): a caller that tests «= 0» cannot take it for a full green.
    • SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP stop the running check and mark the remaining ones BLOCKED (aborted).
    • The limits of the run calls add up to 17,860 s (about 4 h 58 min). That is a ceiling, not a measured duration; with RX_TEMPO=2 it is 35,720 s. The only measured whole round on record is the one of the release package on the GNOME virtual machine: 47 min (docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md).
    i
    No layout difference. fresh.sh looks for box.sh in prove/boxes/ and, if that folder is not there, in the top-level boxes/: it works from a plain checkout. lib.py does the same with its BOXES variable. The warning that the Debian manual carried about a layout difference does not apply to fresh.sh in this tree; matrix.sh has no mention of boxes and calls fresh.sh, so it follows.

    17.5 · The package check

    check-package.py tests the .deb itself on a box that it may reset freely. It is not in all.sh: it resets the box at the start (and again for the refusal check) and at the end leaves it fresh, with the package installed and the service enabled (fresh.sh), so it must not run on a box somebody else is testing. A VM cannot be reset by the bench (banco-vm/box.sh refuses reset), so the check never runs on the VM bench.

    !
    Not aligned with the new postinst. The check was last aligned with the file list of Debian. Its install step lists as expected only /var/lib/remotix, /run/remotix and /etc/apparmor.d/local/remotix_network among the paths that no package owns; the system dconf database /etc/dconf/db/remotix, which the postinst makes and which has remotix in its name, is owned by no package, so by the reading of c_install() the step would report it as an unexpected file wherever dconf-cli is installed (it is a Recommends, so almost everywhere). This is a reading of the code: the check was not run on Ubuntu 26.04 and the manual does not claim it passes or fails. It is for the coordinator to decide whether to add the path to the check.

    What the package contains and how its scripts behave is in ch. 15 “The package”.

    17.6 · The four test boxes

    The container boxes are four systemd containers, one per desktop, built from one boxes/Containerfile with --build-arg DESKTOP=gnome|kde|xfce|lxqt. There is NOTHING of REMOTIX inside the image: the package is installed later with apt, so the box is what a user's machine looks like before the install. This is not the bench of the release: it is the bench of the rounds of 18 and 19 Nov 2026 and of the first hand tests, and it is still in the tree. On the owner's order of 19 Nov 2026 the four containers and their images were deleted from the dev server, and the bench of the release is the VM bench (17.8 “The VM bench”); the package is no longer built in a container either (ch. 18 “Build and release”). The boxes can be rebuilt with boxes/box.sh build; server/prepara-server.sh prepares the server for them.

    boxes/box.sh is the only entry point. Verbs: build (image; it generates the ssh key box-key, which is not in git), boot, shutdown, status, ssh (a command as root inside, over ssh on 127.0.0.1), install (copy the .deb in, refresh the package lists as on a real machine, run apt-get install -y --reinstall so that a package of the same version replaces the files too, then write REMOTIX_PORT=<port> into /etc/remotix/remotix.conf.d/10-box-port.conf because the default 7447 would clash between boxes), and reset (throw the container away and boot a fresh one from the image). The service is left as the package leaves it: disabled and not started; fresh.sh enables it.

    How a box is built and started

    • The desktop as an Ubuntu user installs it. The metapackage of the flavour with its Recommends: ubuntu-desktop-minimal, kubuntu-desktop, xubuntu-desktop or lubuntu-desktop, after the display manager of that desktop has been stated to debconf. boxes/set-dm.sh then registers the manager as its postinst would on a real machine (a container build does not do it): /etc/X11/default-display-manager and the enabled unit with its display-manager.service alias. It fails if the registration is not there at the end.
    • No snap, and a desktop that is not GNOME has no GNOME. snapd does not run in a container, so an apt preference at -1 keeps out firefox, thunderbird and chromium-browser (on Ubuntu they are wrappers of snaps; the browser of the tests is on the server). For Kubuntu, Xubuntu and Lubuntu a second preference keeps out gnome-shell, gdm3 and ubuntu-session, because the bare xubuntu-desktop brings gdm3 as the default manager and a flavour from its ISO has no GNOME (box finding BOX-01, studio/8-pacchetto-e-prove.md). The image's own user ubuntu (uid 1000) is removed, so that prova and prova2 get uid 1000 and 1001 as on a fresh install; the build fails otherwise.
    • Identity check. boxes/box-identity.sh is run during the image build as box-identity ubuntu 26.04 <de> -: an image that is not Ubuntu 26.04 with that desktop, its display manager and its session files is not built.
    • systemd as init. --systemd=always, host network (so every box has its own ports), all of /dev/dri, memlock unlimited (low-memory-monitor on GNOME calls mlockall), the capabilities a real login needs (AUDIT_WRITE, AUDIT_CONTROL, SYS_ADMIN, SYS_NICE, WAKE_ALARM) and a pids limit of 16384. boot waits up to 120 s for systemd to be running and 90 s for ssh.
    • No display manager runs. boxes/common.sh sets the default target to multi-user.target (the box has no monitor), configures sshd on 127.0.0.1 and on the box's port, makes the journal persistent (512 MB cap) and installs box-gruppi, which aligns the box's video and render groups with the groups of the host's DRM nodes (in a box they arrive with the host's numbers).
    • Sleep questions answered as on a real machine. boxes/power.sh (run at every boot) mounts a tmpfs copy of /sys/power and restarts logind: in a container /sys is read-only and logind would answer "Call failed" before asking polkit, so the polkit rule of the package would not be what is tested. The real /sys/power is not touched. It also removes /etc/systemd/sleep.conf.d/remotix-no-suspend.conf if present and restarts logind each time, so it must not be run on a machine whose administrator switched that belt on.
    • Test users. Two ordinary users, prova and prova2, with the password of the Containerfile (no sudo). The checks make their own.
    • KDE. The Plasma Welcome Center is hidden for new users through /etc/skel so that it does not cover a first login.

    The boxes share the host's kernel, network and DRM nodes, which has two known consequences. Xwayland display numbers and their abstract sockets are shared, and docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md records 33 X screens in all as a limit when many containers run: this is why lib.Compositor runs the test compositor in its own network and mount namespace. And inotify limits are shared by one uid, so server/prepara-server.sh raises fs.inotify.max_user_instances to 8192 and fs.inotify.max_user_watches to 1048576. The podman storage is shared with the Debian work: prepara-server.sh keeps it under /media/REMOTIX-DEBIAN/podman (the variable PODMAN_BASE) and writes the configuration files only if they are absent.

    i
    Stale comments. Some comment headers in boxes/power.sh and boxes/box-identity.sh may still describe other distributions and the old bench scripts (17-box.sh, 11-box-power.sh); they were not re-read for this manual, and the code that runs is the one of the two files.

    17.7 · The real-system virtual machine

    A container shares the host's kernel, has no real boot and no real device model. For what only a whole machine shows, server/vm.sh runs a real Ubuntu 26.04 under KVM. It is the first of the two VM scripts of the tree; the second, server/vm-radeon.sh, is the bench of the release (17.8 “The VM bench”).

    server/vm-login-test.py opens the page of the REMOTIX in that VM (127.0.0.1:8901) with the Chrome driver of prove/lib.py (imported, not modified) and logs in as prova. It touches no box: the Rig's box is replaced by a stub, because lib.Box would run commands in the test containers. It prints facts and exits 0 if the login reached a session; --bad uses a wrong password. Its sys.path entry names /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/prove, whereas the corresponding script of the Radeon machines, server/vm-radeon-login-test.py, names /media/REMOTIX-UBUNTU/albero/prove: which of the two folders holds lib.py on the server was not checked for this manual.

    What this machine can and cannot show: it has no real card, so the server says CANNOT ENCODE VIDEO and no session shows a picture; it has the real boot, the real kernel, the real AppArmor and the real package scripts. No result of a run on it is recorded in the logs read for this manual; the machine of the first round of the Debian manual (installation, AppArmor, reboot, removal and purge without leftovers) has no Ubuntu equivalent in the records.

    17.8 · The VM bench

    The container boxes could not show what a real Ubuntu does: the profile of AppArmor is not in force in a container, no snap runs there, and a display manager does not run. The first real machine (a live Ubuntu 26.04.1, 19 Nov 2026) found two defects in an afternoon, C4 and C5, that the container rounds had not (17.12 “What was verified on Ubuntu 26.04, and what was not”). The bench that followed is four QEMU virtual machines, one per flavour, installed from the desktop image of the flavour and handed the server's Radeon card by passthrough, with the checks of prove/ adapted to run against them, and a fifth machine that only builds the package (18.1 “The build of the .deb on the build VM”). It is the bench of the release. There are no containers on it: tests and studies run on virtual machines only. The scripts are server/vm-radeon.sh, server/prepara-server-vm.sh and prove/banco-vm/; server/VM-BANCO.md is the note that goes with them.

    The four machines

    Why three disks are not an autoinstall: Kubuntu and Lubuntu come with Calamares, and the live kernel of Xubuntu crashed the installer (a kernel oops, recorded in docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md and in the comment of the script). crea then builds the disk by hand: a GPT partition table with a 512 MB EFI partition and an ext4 root, the layers of the ISO unpacked one over the other with rsync, then a stage run in a chroot (fstab, hostname, an empty machine-id so that a new one is made at the first boot, the users prova (with sudo) and prova2, the installer's own removals, the bootloader packages from the ISO pool, openssh-server, the initramfs, grub-install --no-nvram so that the server's firmware variables are never touched), and converts the raw image to qcow2. The temporary raw image is the only thing the script deletes, and only after the qcow2 exists. The four test machines have a 40 GB disk, 12 GB of memory and 8 CPUs with the Radeon (5 GB and 4 CPUs without it; RX_VM_MEM overrides the memory), q35 with UEFI (OVMF), KVM and the host CPU, no display, a serial console in serial.log, and user networking with the ports of the table forwarded (ssh, and REMOTIX over TCP and UDP). The kernel of the Ubuntu machine was 7.0.0-44-generic at the release run.

    server/vm-radeon.sh

    One lock file serialises the commands: a second call while a VM is being started, stopped or built is refused with «another vm-radeon.sh holds the lock», and the scripts below retry. The Radeon is one, so one VM at a time has it; the four desktops are tried one after the other, and the change of machine is spegni of one then accendi of the other (about 5 s and 18 s, docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md). While a VM holds the card the containers cannot use it either. The script runs as a user that can use sudo, because QEMU and vfio need root.

    The server preparation and the kernel parameter that the Radeon machines need

    The dev server's root file system is in RAM. After every reboot prepara-server-vm.sh is run first (no podman, no container): it puts back QEMU, OVMF, the disk tools, the kernel modules loop, squashfs and vfio-pci, an ACL that lets the user open /dev/kvm, the browsers and tools of the checks, a sound server for Firefox (PipeWire with a null sink) and the inotify limits, and the server side of the Radeon protection: the kernel log written to disk line by line, vfio-pci with disable_idle_d3=1 (in /etc/modprobe.d/remotix-vfio.conf; a loaded module with another value is reloaded when nobody uses it, otherwise the step says FAIL) and power/control=on for the card and the PCI bridges above it. It prints one OK or FAIL line per step and the values it read back.

    The rule. On 26 Nov 2026 the dev server froze four times because the amdgpu driver in a guest put the passed-through Radeon to sleep (that was on the Debian machines, with kernel 6.12). The rule is now in the script, whoever runs it, and it is kept on the Ubuntu bench too. crea writes amdgpu.runpm=0 on the guest's kernel command line (/etc/default/grub.d/zz-remotix-banco.cfg, named to sort last so that no other 99-* file can undo it) and fails if the parameter is missing at the first boot. accendi with the Radeon needs a marker, runpm.ok, written only after the machine, started WITHOUT the Radeon, showed the parameter in /proc/cmdline; the marker is good for ONE boot, so every accendi with the Radeon is preceded by a fresh proof (15 to 30 s more). If the marker is missing the script makes that virtual start itself, applies the parameter if needed, reboots and checks again; with no proof it refuses and the card is not given. There is no option to skip the check. After the start with the Radeon, /sys/module/amdgpu/parameters/runpm must read 0 and the parameter must be in /proc/cmdline (read three times); otherwise the machine is switched off at once and the card given back. Only one machine of the whole server may hold the Radeon. No freeze happened in the sessions of 26 and 27 Nov 2026 (register G1).

    The scripts around it

    The adapted round

    The checks of prove/ do not know they are on a VM except through three things. RX_BANCO=vm makes lib.py look for box.sh in prove/banco-vm/ and use the ports 8841 to 8844. RX_TEMPO multiplies every deadline (all.sh sets it to 2 when RX_BANCO=vm and nothing else is given). And the --box names stay gnome, kde, xfce, lxqt: gnome is the machine ubuntu, kde is kubuntu, xfce is xubuntu, lxqt is lubuntu.

    • banco-vm/box.sh has the face of boxes/box.sh. ssh runs the command as root over ssh with the bench key; it does not use sudo, because sudo writes every command line, including the secrets typed by a check, into the VM's journal, and check-ban.py then rightly found a typed name in the journal. rootkey puts the public key of the machine in /root/.ssh/authorized_keys once per VM, through prova and sudo (the only use of sudo there); it is idempotent and says «bench key installed for root» when it had to write it. The key stays in the VM. install copies the .deb in and runs apt-get install -y --reinstall; there is no 10-box-port.conf, the VM keeps 7447 inside and the host forwards 884x. status lists the four machines. reset refuses.
    • banco-vm/fresh-vm.sh is the clean state of a VM that stays on (a VM cannot be thrown away and recreated by the bench, and ripristina needs it off). It checks the identity (Ubuntu 26.04 and the display manager of that desktop), stops the service, ends the sessions of the test users and deletes them with their homes (never prova, prova2 or any other name), removes the checks' own drop-ins, renames a non-empty ban file to ban.fresh-<time> (kept, not deleted), installs with apt the tools the container image had if they are missing (after simulating: if it would upgrade or remove a package already there, nothing is installed and it is a FAIL, for the owner to decide), hides the Welcome Center in /etc/skel on KDE, and starts the service again. It checks its own work: a test user, a process of theirs or the service still there is a FAIL. It is not equivalent to a container reset: the rest of the disk stays as it was (files in /tmp and /var, the journal, snap state, anything an earlier run left outside the list).
    • The initial control of all.sh on a VM. After the bench key is in place, all.sh sends 300,000 random bytes through box.sh ssh <de> md5sum and compares the checksum with the local one: the checks send data on stdin to commands in the VM, and it must arrive intact. If it does not, the run does not start (a line FAIL the VM of <de>: stdin through the root ssh is not intact, exit 1). A first form of this control, over sudo -S, stopped the first launches («stdin through sudo -S is not intact», the log vm-gnome-unione8b/summary.txt holds only that line); it was then rewritten for root.
    • SKIP rows. Three things are listed on a VM, never counted as PASS and never as a failure: prelocal/real-login (P7, P8, P9, the real local login with programs open: only with RX_LOCALE_VERO=1), ban/other-addresses (every client reaches the VM as 10.0.2.2, so only that address is banned; the 127.0.0.1 case of the containers does not exist) and package (check-package.py needs a reset a VM cannot do).
    • NOTE rows. The bench key was installed for root; the Welcome Center of KDE was hidden in /etc/skel (it stays for users made by hand too).

    The round of the release package of 19 Nov 2026 on the GNOME machine

    The round vm-gnome-unione10 (tag of the log folder; the package of the release at that moment, still numbered 1.0.0) ran on the ubuntu machine with the Radeon, 47 min. Result: 120 PASS, 2 FAIL, 1 BLOCKED, 3 SKIP (123 verdict rows, 0 NOTE). This complete round is of the package unione10 (polkit rule of 15 actions); the package with the rule of 19 actions, unione11, has the same build checks but had no complete round, only the partial desktop round described above. The seven checks of check-desktop.py that existed then were all there; power-implied and power-local-seat were not. The three lines that are not PASS:

    • desktop/users-shell-and-environment FAIL: known and accepted. The terminal of GNOME is ptyxis and in it SHELL is empty; pkexec then says «The value for the SHELL variable was not found in the /etc/shells file» and the check, which wants pkexec to make the agent ask for a password, fails. It was identical in the container round of 18 Nov 2026 and is listed in the register of problems (E2).
    • ban/typed-names-not-logged FAIL: a false red of the bench. The evidence is the journal of the VM with sudo lines written by the bench's own commands, among them the grep for the secret that the check had typed. The bench was changed to enter as root with a key (above). Re-run after the change, ban gave 8 of 8 PASS (log vm-gnome-rootfix/, a partial round with --only ban,audio-firefox: 9 PASS in all).
    • audio-firefox BLOCKED: ToolError: no answer from Marionette in 45 s. The test Firefox was mute at its first start; the tool could not look, which is BLOCKED and not FAIL. Repeated, it gave PASS, twice (vm-gnome-rootfix/ and vm-gnome-rootfix-af2/).
    • The 3 SKIP rows are the three above.

    Limits of this record. The round of 19 Nov 2026 was run once, on one machine of the four; after the change of the bench to root, the complete round was not run again, only ban and audio-firefox (docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md says so). The complete rounds of 1.2.0 on all four machines are the next block.

    The rounds of 1.2.0 (26 and 27 November 2026)

    • The automatic round (all.sh with RX_BANCO=vm, one machine at a time with the Radeon): GNOME 125 PASS and 1 known FAIL (desktop/users-shell-and-environment, SHELL empty with pkexec); KDE, XFCE and LXQt 126 PASS (register G3). The first round of 26 Nov 2026 found three faults of the tools, all corrected in the checks and none in the product: check-resilience.py read as its result a warning of systemd (unit file changed on disk) on service-restart (XFCE); unit_residue of check-prelocal.py counted gnome-keyring-daemon.service as a leftover of the remote desktop although a local login starts it too (Xubuntu); check-desktop.py read a panel file at the path of Debian (LXQt).
    • The real local login with programs open (P7 and P9 on all four desktops; P8 on Kubuntu and Xubuntu, BLOCKED by construction on GNOME and LXQt): all PASS. On Kubuntu the editor (kate) closed gently in 5.03 s and then by force, as designed; on Lubuntu the gentle close took about 0.6 s and the local desktop (openbox) was there after 4 s. check-exit.py passed its three cases on XFCE and LXQt, and check-kde-exit.py on KDE, with the desktop just born included.
    • Update and removal: the update from the published 1.0.1 to 1.2.0 and the removal (purge) left the four machines clean.
    • The owner's hand tests on the four VMs (27 Nov 2026): all OK.
    • Not explained: one failure of mouse and keyboard (check-base) on GNOME right after an update with a desktop open, not reproduced; the abnormal ends of wireplumber on all desktops, of kwin_wayland once on Kubuntu at the stop of the service and of xdg-desktop-portal-kde once on Lubuntu (register H3 and H4).

    Snapshots

    The snapshots are internal qcow2 snapshots of the disk. The names that the records show: pulito (clean, after the installation of the flavour), aggiornato (after vm-radeon-aggiorna.sh), unione6 and unione10 (the machine just after the installation of that build of the package). The control of 19 Nov 2026 took each machine back to the state «just installed with the release package» before the hand tests. A snapshot does not hold the UEFI variables. For 1.2.0 the machines were handed to the owner clean, to be opened in the browser.

    What was done by hand on real machines

    • The four VMs, by the owner, 27 Nov 2026, with the 1.2.0 package: all OK (register G3). The four VMs, by the owner, 19 Nov 2026, with the package of that evening (numbered 1.0.0): GNOME, KDE, XFCE and LXQt all OK, including detach and reattach from Linux and from Android (docs/STORIA-ubuntu-26.04.md). Noted and not blocking: an «internal error» notice of Ubuntu that is wireplumber stopping at the end of the user's session (seen also after leaving REMOTIX; whether it depends on the VM having no audio card is not known); small stutters in the video seen by Chrome on Android (register E4). The silence from the telephone on Kubuntu was another program on the tablet that carried the telephone's audio elsewhere, not a defect.
    • The four live systems, by the owner, 19 Nov 2026: Ubuntu 26.04.1 (kernel 7.0), Kubuntu 26.04.1 (7.0.0-30), Xubuntu 26.04 and Lubuntu 26.04, each started from the live image of a USB stick on the server itself, the package installed with apt install and systemctl enable --now remotix (the way live-installa.sh does it). On Ubuntu: the login worked at the first attempt, the line «§5.1 … CONNECTED» was in the log, no Unknown DConf source in the journal, the installer of the live started in the remote session without error. On Kubuntu: the login worked at the first attempt, the profile was loaded, labwc and dconf-cli came from apt as Recommends, and the video went through VA-API on the real card (HEVC: yes via vaapi), where the VMs use the Vulkan road: both encoding roads were exercised, on different benches. On Xubuntu: «everything seems to work» (the owner's words); on Lubuntu: OK. The logs of those two live systems were not read.
    • «Local excludes remote», by hand, on the live Ubuntu and the live Kubuntu. A local login at the greeter, with the remote desktop open: the login is held in PAM, the client is sent away with 0x04, the remote desktop is closed, and then the local login goes on. On GNOME the remote desktop closed in 851 ms and the runtime dconf profile was removed in the same second; after the local Log Out a new remote login worked. On KDE the desktop was closed by its own child in 10.9 s (against 0.85 s on GNOME: the closing time of KDE that the register describes in section D). It was not tried at the greeters of Xubuntu and Lubuntu.
    i
    One card. The server's cards: the live systems and the VMs use the same Radeon, so «a real card» in this chapter always means that one. The VMs encode through the Vulkan road, as the first line of the server's start says HEVC: yes via vulkan; the live Kubuntu through VA-API. Intel and NVIDIA cards were not tried on Ubuntu 26.04.

    17.9 · The tools of the 1.2.0 work

    The 1.2.0 work added scripts and checks that are not all in all.sh. Each was written for one question and is run by hand or by a small script.

    Why check-prelocal.py has P7, P8 and P9: a check that opens an empty remote desktop only ever runs the orderly close, so the forced road, the one that stops a desktop with a program still open, was never asked. P7, P8 and P9 open a desktop with a terminal running top, with an editor holding unsaved text and with the snap Firefox, and then make a real local login. Ubuntu has what the other distributions do not: the snap program runs in its own transient scope, so P9 also asks that no snap.firefox.firefox-<uuid>.scope and no firefox process are left. The case looks for new crashes of the user with coredumpctl where systemd-coredump is installed (Kubuntu) and in /var/crash where apport is (the other three); apport records not every crash, so that line is a hint and not a proof of «none», and the result line says which of the two was looked at.

    i
    Allowed on Ubuntu. The cases that restart the display manager inside a machine with the Radeon passed through are forbidden on the Debian bench (the server froze). On the Ubuntu bench the owner allowed them on 26 Nov 2026, with the protection of 17.8 “The VM bench” in force (studio/prove-1.2.0/COME-SI-LANCIA.md).

    17.10 · Testing the real machine from a live USB

    A virtual machine is not the machine: the display manager, the video card and the timings of a real boot are different. The owner therefore also tries the product on a real machine started from a live image of Ubuntu 26.04.1 (Ubuntu, Kubuntu, Xubuntu, Lubuntu), one image per flavour. The package is put in with server/live-installa.sh, run as root from the live terminal and served from another machine on the same network, and the trial is by hand: a remote desktop of the user prova is opened with programs inside, then the same user logs in at the machine, and the remote desktop must close and the local one start.

    • What the script does (numbered steps, re-runnable): initial checks (it stops with a clear message when the network is missing; it warns if the system is not Ubuntu 26.04); downloads the .deb and its .sha256 and refuses to go on if they differ; turns universe on if it is off; apt-get install -y --reinstall of the package with what it recommends; creates the two test users prova and prova2 if they do not exist (it never touches an existing one, nor its password); systemctl enable --now remotix. Apart from universe and the two users it does what the user manual asks of the administrator.
    • The name of the package is a variable at the head of the script (PACCHETTO): remotix_1.2.0-1+ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb.
    • What was tried (the owner, 27 Nov 2026, four live images 26.04.1 on a real machine): Ubuntu, Kubuntu and Xubuntu OK; Lubuntu OK after the point of register H7 was understood. On all four the local login closes the remote desktop of the same user; the local desktop starts a few seconds later, the time to close the remote one in order (seen by the owner and accepted). On the Lubuntu live image the remote desktop takes the settings folder of the installer's session (/etc/xdg/xdg-lubuntu-live-environment, the «Try or install» screen) and not the one of the normal session: icons missing and the panel complete only after about a minute (local_session_name_find() in src/session.c). It does not happen on the installed system, where the installer declares the normal session (a Lubuntu virtual machine had icons and panel in order); the owner decided to leave it as it is. From then on the trials on a real machine are made with a distribution installed on a USB stick, not on a live image.

    The rule that comes out of the Fedora work holds here too: on a new distribution or desktop, the trial «the local login closes the remote one» is made with programs open in the remote desktop, on a real machine, before publishing.

    17.11 · What only a real machine or a real phone can prove

    Each item below is something no file in prove/ or server/ can show, with the reason.

    +
    Tip. A statement in this manual that depends on one of the rows above is marked as not verified where it appears.

    The lesson of the containers

    Two defects of the Ubuntu work, C4 (every sign-in refused) and C5 (snap and Flutter programs), were invisible on the container bench for reasons that are written in the tree: a container does not exercise AppArmor and has no snap. A bench that does not run a protection cannot show that the protection is wrong, and it shows green. The rule that came out of it (register C4): before closing a port to a new distribution, a login must succeed on a real machine, or a virtual one, with AppArmor (or SELinux) in force, and the log line «§5.1 … CONNECTED» must be read. The second lesson (B3-bis): when the same line is red on all four desktops while it was green on the earlier distribution, suspect the tool and look at the raw events first. Three lines (mouse-drag in two browsers and tap-and-half-drag-select) failed identically everywhere, and the cause was the test window, not the product (GTK 4.22, above).

The package of the container and first VM rounds is remotix_1.0.0-1+ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb in successive builds (the work called them unione1 to unione10, and then unione11); the one of the 1.2.0 rounds is remotix_1.2.0-1+ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb. The name of a build does not matter here, the checks quoted are named with the build that ran them.
